Each piece is made to order by hand in California, with a choice of fabrics and finishes, and the studio also designs custom furniture for commercial and residential projects. The collection includes the Piazza and Ricard chairs, the Madda sectional and the Pascal modular sofa. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:nedrefoss.name: Nedrefoss
paragraphs: Nedre Foss is a Norwegian brand of homeware objects, directed by the design studio Anderssen & Voll. It is built on the idea of the Century Product, an object meant to serve for at least 100 years, where sculptural qualities and utility count equally.

Most pieces are designed by Anderssen & Voll, with others by Studio Sløyd, Julie Richoz, Jin Kuramoto and Carina Seth Andersson. They include the Knubb tray in solid ash, the Laguz household weight in cast iron, the Anker candlestick and the Vannfall water jug in mould-blown glass. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Homeware in ash, cast iron and glass

makers:nicholas-bijan-pourfard.name: Nicholas Bijan Pourfard
paragraphs: Nicholas Bijan Pourfard is a furniture and lighting designer based in Southern California, with a San Diego address, who designs and crafts furniture and functional objects. Pieces are made to order in six to eight weeks unless otherwise specified.

Seating and tables are hand-built in wood, such as the Box Chair, the Loop Table and the Anything Bench, whose backrests swivel separately. Lamps use hand-blown glass draped over handmade metal bases, as in the Bloop table lamp and sconce. On Formground their work is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:patrick-de-glo-de-besses.name: Patrick de Glo de Besses
paragraphs: Patrick de Glo de Besses designs and makes chairs, each listed as work by the designer and marked Paris, Les collections, with a year from 2022 to 2026. The chairs are built in solid wood, either with spruce legs and box-like seats and backrests in stained maritime pine, or carved from a single oak plank and assembled with joinery.

Trapèze II is a solid oak chair with a backrest bevelled into a trapezoid, Oratorio has a backrest of curved and quarter-round shapes, and Dorsale rests a two-board backrest on a central spine. The Box series, such as Box IV, uses box-like seats. On Formground their work is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:wontek.name: Wontek
paragraphs: Wontek is a product design brand based in Warsaw, Poland. It designs and 3D-prints lamps, vases and decorative objects, treating 3D printing as a modern form of weaving, where each layer works like a thread that builds colour, pattern and texture.

Every piece is printed, finished and packed in the Warsaw studio, which allows a colour, a pattern or a whole form to be changed for a single order. The range includes the Mirage lamps, the Weave lamp and boxes, and the Afterloom vase. The name plays on the Polish word wątek, meaning thread or weft. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:studio-vraco.name: Studio Vraco
paragraphs: Studio Vraco is a family-owned brand of furniture and home objects, with its head office and all manufacturing in Visoko, Bosnia and Herzegovina. It grew out of Vraco, a metalwork business founded in 1975 by Ibrahim Vraco, and was created by Mirsad Vraco and his daughter Emina Vraco.

The pieces combine metal, stone and wood with Bosnian craft traditions, and the studio works with designers from Scandinavia and elsewhere. The TSD x SV collections include console tables, a sofa table, a stool, vases, a box and trays. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Furniture and objects in wood, metal and stone

makers:shibui.name: Shibui
paragraphs: Shibui is a homeware and accessories company based in Carouge, Switzerland, created by the designers Constantinos Hoursoglou from Switzerland and Athanasios Babalis from Greece. The name is a Japanese word for an aesthetic of simple, unobtrusive beauty.

The objects are handmade in Europe by specialist artisans and include the Linelight desk lamp, the Pinch container, the Float shelving, the Spice salt and pepper set and the iceCube wine cooler. The company is moving towards small-batch special editions and gradually discontinuing most of its existing line. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:juntos-projects.name: Juntos Projects
paragraphs: Juntos Projects is a design studio in New York, led by María Daniela Huiza and Abraham Bendheim, that explores form, colour and material. The name is the Spanish word for together. Every piece is made in the Northeast of the United States with skilled craftspeople, in natural materials.

Colours are mixed by hand and layered so that grain and end cuts stay visible. The collection includes the Arc stool and bench, the Raja chair, the Isos lounge chair, the Marquise dining table and the Mortise shelving system. The studio received an ICFF Editors' Award in 2024. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Furniture and objects in natural materials

makers:tlachi-design.name: Tlachï Design
paragraphs: Tlachï Design is a Mexican furniture maker that designs and builds seating and tables in Guadalajara for outdoor and indoor use, in restaurants, hotels and homes. The frames are steel with electrostatic paint, and seats and sides are woven in olefin rope or covered in outdoor fabric.

The Mono bench is woven by hand by artisans in Querétaro, and the Tapatía chair reinterprets the traditional Mexican equipal. Other pieces include the Nodo chair and Vano table from the tlachï x rosco collection, the Mono stool and the Santa Fe sofa. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Outdoor and indoor furniture in steel and rope

makers:kieran-kinsella.name: Kieran Kinsella
paragraphs: Kieran Kinsella is a sculptor and furniture maker based in New York's Hudson Valley. The wood pieces are stump stools and tables carved from tree trunks, using locally sourced and salvaged Northeast hardwoods that are hand carved and kiln-dried.

The ceramic stools and side tables are made in slip-cast porcelain and hand-built stoneware, using the original wood pieces as moulds and models. Forms include Bulb, Kettle, Macaroni Bench, Cloud Bench, Cauldron and Drop. On Formground their work is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Carved wood and ceramic stools, benches and tables

makers:h-bigeleisen.name: H. Bigeleisen
paragraphs: H. Bigeleisen is the design practice of Hannah Bigeleisen, who designs sculptural furniture and lighting in Brooklyn, New York. The practice was founded in 2020, after the first lighting collection debuted at Brooklyn Designs, and is guided by a background in sculpture.

The work includes the Clover pouf, the Sunny Side Up sconce, and the Stack, Blob, IO and Fringe lamps. Most of it is made to order, and studio visits are by appointment only. On Formground their work is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:avolt.name: Avolt
paragraphs: Avolt is a Swedish design studio, founded by Johan Runströmer in 2018, that develops and designs objects which extend electricity to devices. The aim is power solutions for homes, offices and shops that fit in with the architecture and interior.

The pieces include Lamp 1, an LED socket light, Square 1, a power extender, Square 2, a wall-mounted power extender, and Cable 1. The studio has a showroom in Stockholm for architects and design professionals. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Power extenders, cables and a socket light

makers:will-choui.name: Will Choui
paragraphs: Will Choui is a Montreal-based furniture designer whose work draws on raw materials, platonic solids and the rugged presence of brutalist architecture. All pieces are designed and manufactured in Canada.

The 1980 collection takes the structured look of 1980s corporate interiors, with smoked glass diffusers and geometric grids. The WCL lounge chair began as a single 8-foot length of 2x4 lumber and is now made in hand-polished tubular stainless steel as an editioned work. Other pieces include the Alu side table and the Squarehead mirror. On Formground their work is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:studio-mignone.name: Studio Mignone
paragraphs: Studio Mignone makes original sculptural furniture and objects. The Tavolo Morbido coffee table has pillars handcrafted from resin and finished in high gloss or satin, topped with painted or clear 6mm glass.

The Chewing gum chess set is hand cast in pigmented resin, with squashed chewing gum for pawns. Pieces are handcrafted in Australia and made to order, with lead times of about six to eight weeks. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Sculptural furniture and objects in resin

makers:ruka-studio.name: Ruka Studio
paragraphs: Ruka Studio is a collective of former Apple engineers and designers making products for the home around the idea of ritual. Its first product is the Ruka TD-1, a vertical record player that can be mounted on a wall, set on a floor stand or placed on a tabletop.

The TD-1 plays wirelessly to modern speakers or as pure analog through a hi-fi. It is machined from aluminium, has knobs that turn and switches that click, and seats the record with a magnetic clamp. One of its designers, who spent five years at Apple, trained at ArtCenter and works in Los Angeles. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:esther-knopfler.name: Esther Knopfler
paragraphs: Esther Knopfler designs limited-edition marble furniture, handcrafted in the South of France and in Italy together with artisans whose families have worked Italian marble for generations. Each piece takes three to four months to make, and her work has gone to private homes across Europe, the US and the Middle East.

The collections are Wriggle, Cor, Roll, Strata, Saint Lambert and Burger, with pieces such as the Aïmi and Sun dining tables, the Perle console and the Strata stool. On Formground their work is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Marble tables, consoles, seating and lighting

makers:editions-midi.name: Editions Midi
paragraphs: Éditions Midi is a Marseille house for Provençal furniture and ceramics, begun in 2019 by interior architect Jérémie du Chaffaut, a Penninghen graduate who had designed boutiques for luxury houses. He works with a ceramicist near Aix-en-Provence and with a chair maker in the Camargue, using oak from managed forests and rush from the banks of the Rhône.

Pieces include the Radassié oak bench, the Fautuei and Cadiero seats with rush seating, and the hand-turned Bugadiero and Counsciènci ceramics. A design studio, Midi Studio, takes bespoke interior projects. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:farrah-sit.name: Farrah Sit
paragraphs: Farrah Sit designs lighting, furniture and sculptural home objects, with a process built on material reduction and natural elements such as stone, ceramic, marble and brass. She is also the founder of Light + Ladder, a home décor brand whose ceramics are made in Vermont.

Her lighting includes the Serpentine and Cono sconces, the Maillage pendant, the Scorpio and Hathor table lamps, and the Satin Khora chandelier. She has made collections with CB2, TRNK and Tortuga, and takes licensing and custom projects. On Formground their work is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:b-line-italia.name: B-Line Italia
paragraphs: B-Line is an Italian furniture company founded by Giorgio Bordin, whose path began in 1999 by recovering original moulds and reissuing design pieces from the 1960s and 1970s, among them Joe Colombo's Boby storage trolley. Beside the reissues it makes contemporary products designed by Tommaso Caldera, Maddalena Casadei, Michael Geldmacher and Zanellato/Bortotto.

All production is in Italy, and moulds from the seventies are still in use. The company is based in Sarmeola di Rubano, in the province of Padua. Tables such as 4/4, Fonda and AD.DA and the Esa seating are part of the range. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Reissued design icons, tables, seating and accessories

makers:mike-ruiz-serra.name: Mike Ruiz-Serra
paragraphs: The shop Mike Serra Studio sells furniture, lighting, objects and hardware, and its product pages describe them as made to order with a lead time of eight to twelve weeks. The SkinFrame lighting family of pendant, sconce, table lamp and floor lamp is built in aluminium and fibre paper, with the drop height, paper colour and metal adjustable.

The Gumby Chair combines sand-cast aluminium with bent plywood, and the Speed Hole Table pairs aluminium with solid sapele. Knobs and pulls, a Dutch oven and a ring trivet are also made, and custom orders and international shipments are taken by enquiry. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:sabu-studio.name: Sabu Studio
paragraphs: Sabu Studio is a Melbourne furniture, lighting and object design company founded in 2020 by designer-maker Samuel Burns. Its practice rests on honesty to materials and a contemporary approach to craftsmanship, and all of its furniture and lighting is handmade to order. Custom design is offered alongside the range.

The furniture includes the Lune and Plane cabinets, the Tide and Twenty tables, the Etto and Twenty chairs and the Arc bench. Lighting includes the Miro sconce, the Vale and Tier pendants and the Onu pendants. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:utilitario-mexicano.name: Utilitario Mexicano
paragraphs: Utilitario Mexicano is a Mexico City brand run by a married couple who search out and select everyday Mexican objects, and who have gathered more than 1,500 of them. Many are low-technology utensils from workshops for metalwork, carpentry, turning and ceramics, some of them made again exclusively for the brand.

The ceramics shown here include the Salero Máscara and Diablito en arcilla, the Chango en arcilla, porcelain cups and plates, and the Set Los Compas. The shop is on Calle Marsella in Colonia Juárez. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:silcohaus.name: Silcohaus
paragraphs: Silcohaus was founded in Sydney in 2023 by Alan and Vivi as an editorial and curation platform around colour, material and light. It brings together work by other designers and studios and also makes pieces through its in-house Studio Silco, which began with the Noka lamp and includes the Arno lamps and the Luno side tables.

The selection includes cabinets, sideboards and framed objects by Rayon Belge, the Mo_&_A bamboo floor lamp by HAO, the Volet lamp by S30 and the Hourglass T001 by Gwladys Faye. A showroom in Newtown hosts exhibitions. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:rieul-lighting.name: Rieul Lighting
paragraphs: Rieul Lighting is a Seoul lighting brand that makes its lamps by 3D printing, on the view that new methods of making create new design languages. Its lamps carry names such as Bukchon, Dosan, Myungju and Heugyujae, and it also makes the Seokpa vases.

A Monthly Lighting project has launched a new lamp each month, reaching its sixteenth with the art and design studio Walza. Light of Layers takes the Korean Jogakbo patchwork as its starting point. Pieces are sold through 29CM, Ohou.se and the DDP Design Store. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:objects-for-objects.name: Objects for Objects
paragraphs: Objects for Objects is a Los Angeles furniture and design studio founded in 2017 by Leonard Bessemer, a self-taught carpenter who worked with the sculptor David Thorpe in Berlin. It makes furniture and objects meant to be valued as sculptural objects, with much of the fabrication done in-house and to order.

Production is in small batches, limited editions and pre-orders. The work includes the Rubble Kid's Collection, the Seymour and Mallow lamps, the Sidewall table, the Barney and Magnum kids' chairs, and a Soft Wave bench made with Raf Simons and Kvadrat. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:dzovag-kotchian.name: Dzovag Kotchian
paragraphs: Dzovag Kotchian makes objects in stabilised raw earth, a manufacturing process developed by letting the material guide the hand, and the work sits between art and design. It comes as limited series, unique pieces for collectors and custom pieces for architects, and the address is Le Cannet, in the south of France.

The collections are Corail, Olympe, Ekho, Totem and Damier, with the Pyramide and Corail lamps, the Perle wall lamp, the Eros and Damier mirrors, the Récif vases and the Héra table. Exhibitions have included Galerie Suzanne, Maison & Objet and the Antibes Art Fair. On Formground their work is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Lamps, mirrors, vases and a table in raw earth

makers:artetica.name: Artetica
paragraphs: Artetica began in Milan in July 2022, when fashion designer Giorgia Conte and architect Sergio Di Pilato joined design, architecture and fashion in one project. The name comes from an Apulian dialect word for a restless urge to keep making. It opened its Milan space in April 2023, during Milan Design Week.

Artetica works as a design brand, with collection and bespoke products, and as a consultancy for interiors and architecture. Primary colours and clean shapes mark the objects, which include the AB vases, the Plissé piece, a candlestick, an ashtray and incense holders. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:kouros-maghsoudi.name: Kouros Maghsoudi
paragraphs: Kouros Maghsoudi was born in a Chicago suburb to parents who ran a women's clothing boutique and Persian rug galleries, and studied sustainable architecture and urban design. His first furniture collection, Mehmooni, draws on his Persian heritage with playful postmodern motifs, and his contact details are in New York.

The pieces shown include the Hug Chair and Hug Bed, the Neo-Lounge Chair, the Dose and Taarof tables, the Doodool Mirror and the Cloud Vessel. They are sold through stockists such as Love House in New York, Boon Room in Paris and 1stDibs. On Formground their work is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:chatterton-studio.name: Chatterton Studio
paragraphs: Chatterton Studio is the practice of husband and wife Isaac and Alex Chatterton. Isaac, who trained in furniture design and making and apprenticed for two years in upstate New York under Joshua Vogel, leads design and making, while Alex, a graphic designer, shapes the studio's direction and presentation.

The studio works only in solid timber, typically American cherry, oak, ash and walnut, with old machinery and traditional tooling. It shows six candle holders, the Pyramid table and chair, the Providore low table and the Little Chair, and accepts a small number of commissions. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:known-work.name: Known Work
paragraphs: Known Work is a New York studio founded by Danu Kennedy and Jeremy Levitt, partners in the design firm Parts and Labor Design, with Alex Dilena as creative director. It takes an anthropological approach to each collection, looking at the relationship between people and objects.

The collections are numbered: KW 01 is Perceptions, with a plinth, bench, cube, chair, ottoman, catchall, candle holder and table and floor lamps, KW 02 is a collaboration with Petra, and KW 03 is The Mother. Seating, lighting, tables, plinths, objects and hardware are in the range. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Seating, lighting, tables, plinths and objects

makers:tim-teven-studio.name: Tim Teven Studio
paragraphs: Tim Teven Studio is the practice of the Dutch designer Tim Teven, born in 1993, who founded it in the Netherlands after graduating from the Design Academy Eindhoven in 2018. It works through the mechanical deformation of metal, and Teven comes from a family of blacksmiths.

The Pressure series is hand made in the Netherlands. It covers square and rectangular vases in chrome or zinc plating, and the Pressure Stool and Bench, where a pattern pressed into 2 mm aluminium sheet adds strength. Past clients include Gentle Monster, Rimowa and Stone Island. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:interesting-times-gang.name: Interesting Times Gang
paragraphs: Interesting Times Gang is an interior architecture and product design studio in Stockholm, working with materials such as fossil-free concrete, recycled fishing nets, kelp and oyster shells. Besides interiors, it designs bespoke furniture and objects in recycled and bio-based materials.

Its product line includes the Kelp Chair, the Kelp bar stool and Kelpie low stool, the Shelf Life shelf in oyster shell, the Gigas table, and LIV Tundra, made with Ingridsdotter and Jonas Bohlin. The studio is at Vikingagatan 11. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Furniture and objects in recycled and bio-based materials

makers:frangere-studio.name: Frangere Studio
paragraphs: Frangere Studio is a lighting, furniture and object studio run by designer and maker Carina Webb in Auckland, New Zealand. Its first collection, Fun Guy, takes its forms and colours from wild mushrooms and fungi, with handcrafted stained glass shades made in Carina's home studio and workshop.

The shades are cut by hand from coloured glass, edged in copper foil, soldered and polished. Fun Guy comes as a wall sconce, table lamp, floor lamp and pendant. Every piece is made to order, with a lead time of 12 to 14 weeks. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:jonas-lindholm.name: Jonas Lindholm
paragraphs: Jonas Lindholm is a ceramicist who trained in ceramics and glass at Konstfack from 1990 to 1995, after studying sculpture. His workshop is in the Gustavsberg porcelain factory, and his work is held by the Nationalmuseum and Röhsska museet.

He is one of the 90 members of Konsthantverkarna, a craft shop and gallery in Stockholm that sells his work. The pieces shown are a stackable cup, a cup, a round lidded box and a glossy lidded box. On Formground their work is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:anna-lowenhielm-ceramics.name: Anna Löwenhielm Ceramics
paragraphs: Anna Löwenhielm designs and makes ceramics by hand in small series, working in stoneware and porcelain for daily use. Anna holds journeyman's and master's certificates in pottery, the master's being issued by the Swedish Crafts Council, and also teaches ceramics courses in the studio.

Projects include the Varp series with designer Anna von Schewen, the Skogsö series of large hand-thrown stoneware vases in recycled clays, porcelain for a restaurant, and a turned stoneware urn made in 2023 for Stockholm City Hall. A candleholder is shown here. On Formground their work is shown through one piece, linked to its own page.
facts: Stoneware and porcelain for everyday use

makers:sokketz.name: Sokketz
paragraphs: Sokketz is a Swedish company that gives wall switches, dimmers and sockets the colours of the room. It paints the visible plastic parts of ABB Impressivo components, in ten set shades from Dusty Pink and Late Blue to Blackbird and Just White, or in any NCS code on request.

The electrical parts are bought separately from any retailer and sent to Sokketz, then returned painted and ready for an electrician to install. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Painted wall switches, dimmers and sockets
Yes, any NCS colour on request

designers:marie-michielssen.name: Marie Michielssen
paragraphs: Marie Michielssen is a Belgian designer who studied graphic design. Her career began with hand-painted flowerpots, and she has since become part of the in-house design team at Serax, for which she designs two collections a year.

Her work includes ceramic and papier-mâché lighting, the Pawn side tables that double as stools, and the Charly and La Mère tableware lines. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Serax, among them plates, table lamps, side tables, vases and bowls.
facts: Plates, table lamps, side tables, vases, bowls (as shown on Formground)
sources: Serax: A look inside Marie Michielssen's world

designers:jean-baptiste-fastrez.name: Jean-Baptiste Fastrez
paragraphs: Jean-Baptiste Fastrez is a French designer, born in 1984, who lives and works in Paris. He graduated from ENSCI-Les Ateliers in 2010, worked for three years with Ronan and Erwan Bouroullec, and has run his own studio since 2011.

For Galerie kreo he has made limited editions such as the Mask mirrors, Etna coffee tables and Egypt vases, and the Space Craft collection uses straw marquetry and Nextel paint. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo and CVL, among them mirrors, side tables, consoles, coffee tables and ceiling lamps.
facts: Mirrors, side tables, consoles, coffee tables, ceiling lamps (as shown on Formground)

designers:marcello-jori.name: Marcello Jori
paragraphs: Marcello Jori is an Italian artist, born in Merano in 1951, who works as a painter, illustrator and designer. He began exhibiting in 1977 and has shown in galleries and museums in Italy and abroad, including three Venice Biennales.

His design work started in 2007 with the Figure series for Alessi, followed by Christmas ornaments and nativity figures, some made with Massimo Giacon. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them Christmas tree ornaments, ornamental figurines and nativities.
facts: Christmas tree ornaments, ornamental figurines, nativities (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia (Italian): Marcello Jori (birth, career, Alessi from 2007)
Gessato: Marcello Jori (biography, training, Alessi pieces)

designers:francois-bauchet.name: François Bauchet
paragraphs: François Bauchet is a French designer, born in Montluçon in 1948, who trained at the École des Beaux-Arts in Bourges and has taught in Mâcon and Saint-Étienne. His first project, the chair "C'est aussi une chaise", was shown in 1983.

He has worked with Galerie kreo since 1999, and his series there include Module, Hadar, Cellae in technical felt and resin, and Azo in concrete, resin and sand. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them side tables, benches, tables and coffee tables.
facts: Side tables, benches, tables, coffee tables (as shown on Formground)

designers:hee-welling.name: Hee Welling
paragraphs: Hee Welling is a Danish furniture designer based in Copenhagen. He studied at the University of Art and Design in Helsinki, took a master's in furniture design at the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts and set up his own studio in 2003.

He is known for the Hee Collection and the About A series for HAY, and since 2010 he has been a partner in the studio Welling/Ludvik with Icelandic designer Gudmundur Ludvik. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through &Tradition, among them armchairs, dining tables, side chairs, counter tables and bar tables.
facts: Armchairs, dining tables, side chairs, counter tables, bar tables (as shown on Formground)

designers:lorenza-bozzoli.name: Lorenza Bozzoli
paragraphs: Lorenza Bozzoli is an Italian designer, born in Milan, where she studied art at the Brera Academy and still works from a studio. She began in fashion and footwear styling and moved into industrial design in 1996.

Her clients have included Alessi, Moooi, Dedon, Mingardo and Slamp, for which she has designed the La Lollo lighting collection since 2015. In 2013 her Phaedrus chair for Dedon won a European sustainable design award, and in 2018 she founded Lorenza Bozzoli Couture. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Ghidini 1961, Alessi and Mingardo, among them sofas, armchairs, dining tables, ottomans and cabinets.
facts: Sofas, armchairs, dining tables, ottomans, cabinets (as shown on Formground)

designers:gino-sarfatti.name: Gino Sarfatti
paragraphs: Gino Sarfatti was an Italian lighting designer and entrepreneur, born in Venice in 1912. He studied engineering at the University of Genoa and from 1939 devoted himself to lighting through his company Arteluce, which he sold to Flos in 1973.

He won the Compasso d'Oro in 1954 and 1955, and he often designed the bulb arrangement first and then the form around it. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, mostly vintage floor, wall, pendant, ceiling and table lights.
facts: Floor, wall, pendant, ceiling and table lights (as shown on Formground)
sources: Aguttes: Gino Sarfatti (birth, Arteluce, sale to Flos)

designers:nani-marquina.name: Nani Marquina
paragraphs: Nani Marquina is a Spanish rug designer based in Barcelona. She founded nanimarquina in 1987 to bring the rug into contemporary design, and in 1994 moved production to India, where the company works with hand weavers.

The collections include Tres, which celebrates traditional weaving, Bicicleta, made from used bicycle inner tubes, and outdoor rugs in recycled PET fibre, as well as collaborations with Ronan and Erwan Bouroullec and Jaime Hayon. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through nanimarquina, among them indoor and outdoor rugs and poufs.
facts: Indoor and outdoor rugs, indoor and outdoor poufs (as shown on Formground)

designers:note-design-studio.name: Note (design studio)
paragraphs: Note Design Studio is a Swedish design studio based in Stockholm. It was founded in 2008 by Johannes Carlström and Cristiano Pigazzini and works across architecture, interiors, product design, graphic design and design strategy.

Its work includes the Shell Chair for Karl Andersson & Söner and the Void Matters collection for Note Editions, and its site lists projects for Vibia, Mutina and &Tradition. On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fogia, &Tradition, Vibia and Resident, among them side tables, shelving, sofas, table lamps and coffee tables.
facts: Side tables, shelving, sofas, table lamps, coffee tables (as shown on Formground)

designers:david-chipperfield.name: David Chipperfield
paragraphs: David Chipperfield is a British architect, born in London in 1953, who graduated from Kingston School of Art in 1976 and from the Architectural Association in 1977. He founded David Chipperfield Architects in London in 1985 and received the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 2023.

His product design includes the Tonale ceramics for Alessi, which won the Compasso d'Oro in 2011, and the Piana folding chair, acquired by MoMA. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi and Wästberg, among them suspension lamps, table lamps, wall lamps and semi-recessed lamps.
facts: Suspension lamps, table lamps, wall lamps, semi-recessed lamps (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: David Chipperfield (training, practice, Pritzker, product design)

designers:marcel-wanders.name: Marcel Wanders
paragraphs: Marcel Wanders is a Dutch designer, born in Boxtel in 1963, who graduated from the Institute of the Arts Arnhem in 1988. His Knotted Chair brought him attention in the 1990s, and he opened his Amsterdam studio in 2000.

In 2001 he co-founded the design brand Moooi with Casper Vissers, and for Alessi he designed the Dressed tableware in 2011 and the Circus collection in 2016. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi and WonderGlass, among them serving plates, egg cups, containers and chopping boards.
facts: Serving plates, egg cups, containers, chopping boards (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Marcel Wanders (birth, training, studio, Moooi, Alessi)

designers:sami-kallio.name: Sami Kallio
paragraphs: Sami Kallio is a furniture and interior designer born in Helsinki in 1975 who grew up in Sweden and works from a studio in Gothenburg. He learned woodworking techniques such as compression moulding and woodturning, and graduated from the School of Design and Crafts in Gothenburg in 2005.

His work combines Finnish design tradition with Swedish humour. He is best known for the In Between chair and table collection for &Tradition, and showed the collection The Finnish Blood In Me at the Stockholm Furniture Fair. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through &Tradition, among them dining tables, bar tables, coffee tables, counter tables and café tables.
facts: Dining tables, bar tables, coffee tables, counter tables, café tables (as shown on Formground)

designers:sergio-herman.name: Sergio Herman
paragraphs: Sergio Herman is a Dutch chef, born in Oostburg in 1970. He ran Oud Sluis, his father's restaurant, which received three Michelin stars in 2006, and he opened The Jane in Antwerp in 2014.

For Serax he has designed tableware, including the Surface collection and Inku, which was inspired by Japanese ceramics he saw on culinary trips and includes plates, bowls, a coffee and tea set and glassware. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Serax, among them plates, bowls, cups and glasses.
facts: Plates, bowls, cups, glasses (as shown on Formground)

designers:piet-boon.name: Piet Boon
paragraphs: Piet Boon is a Dutch designer who began his career as a contractor. In 1983 he and Karin Meyn founded Studio Piet Boon, which works in exterior, interior and product design from Oostzaan in the Netherlands.

For Serax he has designed the Base range of minimalist bone china dinnerware, cutlery and glassware, the Lumen lighting and scented candles, as well as furniture. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Serax, among them plates, cups, bowls and cutlery.
facts: Plates, cups, bowls, cutlery (as shown on Formground)

designers:luca-nichetto.name: Luca Nichetto
paragraphs: Luca Nichetto is an Italian industrial designer who grew up in Venice and Murano, where his family worked in glass and lighting. He studied industrial design at Università Iuav di Venezia and graduated in 1998.

Nichetto Studio was founded in Venice in 2006 and today works between Venice and Stockholm, covering product and lighting design, furniture, interiors and art direction. Partners include Wittmann, Foscarini and Ginori 1735. The studio's site lists projects and its own editions.
On Formground Luca Nichetto is credited on {count} pieces shown through &Tradition and Fogia, among them lounge chairs, side tables, sofas, chandeliers and coffee tables.
facts: Lounge chairs, side tables, sofas, chandeliers, coffee tables (as shown on Formground)

designers:alvar-aalto.name: Alvar Aalto
paragraphs: Alvar Aalto (1898-1976) was a Finnish architect and designer. He graduated in architecture from the Helsinki University of Technology in 1921 and became known for buildings such as Paimio Sanatorium and Säynätsalo Town Hall.

Aalto treated furniture and lighting as part of a building, aiming for pieces that were practical, attractive and suited to mass production. His bent-plywood work includes the Paimio chair and Stool 60, and the Savoy vase grew out of a 1936 glass design competition. The furniture company Artek was founded in 1935 to produce and sell his designs.
On Formground Alvar Aalto is credited on {count} pieces shown through Artek, among them benches, chairs, tables, stools and storage.
facts: Benches, chairs, tables, stools, storage (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Alvar Aalto (dates, training, Artek founding)

designers:george-sowden.name: George Sowden
paragraphs: George Sowden is a British designer, born in Leeds, who moved to Milan in the early 1970s and works there. He opened his own design and product development studio in 1979 and was a founding member of the Memphis group in 1981.

Over the decades he has developed products for companies worldwide, with a long interest in pattern and decoration. The brand SOWDEN offers lighting objects and home accessories designed in Milan, among them the PL3 portable table lamp. His own site presents work by decade, from the 1970s to today.
On Formground George Sowden is credited on {count} pieces shown through SOWDEN, among them table lamps, ceiling lamps, vases and floor lamps.
facts: Table lamps, ceiling lamps, vases, floor lamps, mills (as shown on Formground)

designers:verner-panton.name: Verner Panton
paragraphs: Verner Panton (1926-1998) was a Danish designer. He studied architecture at the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts in Copenhagen from 1947 to 1951 and worked in Arne Jacobsen's office from 1950 to 1952. In 1963 he moved to Basel in Switzerland.

His work covered furniture, lighting, textiles and complete colour-led interiors, from the Bachelor Chair for Fritz Hansen in 1955 and the Panton Chair to the VP-Europa lamps for Louis Poulsen in 1978. The Verner Panton site presents his rooms, furniture, lamps, textiles and objects.
On Formground Verner Panton is credited on {count} pieces shown through &Tradition, among them pendants, table lamps and floor lamps.
facts: Pendants, table lamps, floor lamps, furniture accessories, canopies (as shown on Formground)

designers:annebet-philips.name: Annebet Philips
paragraphs: Annebet Philips is a Dutch designer who studied Industrial Design Engineering at Delft University of Technology, graduating cum laude. Studio Annebet Philips was set up in Amsterdam in 2013.

The studio works on product and furniture design, including tableware, lighting, chairs and outdoor pieces, through brand collaborations and collectible pieces. Partners named on its site include Serax, Seletti and MOGG. For Serax, Philips designed the Carte Blanche collection, which began as tableware and grew to candle holders and vases.
On Formground Annebet Philips is credited on {count} pieces shown through Serax, among them plates, candle holders, vases and bowls.
facts: Plates, candle holders, vases, bowls (as shown on Formground)

designers:vincent-van-duysen.name: Vincent Van Duysen
paragraphs: Vincent Van Duysen is a Belgian architect and designer, born in 1962 in Lokeren. He studied at the Sint-Lucas School of Architecture in Ghent from 1980 to 1985 and then worked with Aldo Cibic in Milan.

His office, Vincent Van Duysen Architects, is based in Antwerp and works across architecture, interiors, product design and creative direction, with residential and hospitality projects in Europe, the Middle East, Asia and the United States. The office's site lists monographs from 1994 onwards, including the 2024 volume Private.
On Formground Vincent Van Duysen is credited on {count} pieces shown through Serax and WonderGlass, among them dining tables, cups, benches, stools and bar stools.
facts: Dining tables, cups, benches, stools, bar stools (as shown on Formground)
sources: Vincent Van Duysen: home (work areas, monographs)

designers:bela-silva.name: Bela Silva
paragraphs: Bela Silva is a Portuguese ceramicist, born and raised in Lisbon, who splits her time between Lisbon and Brussels. Training took in the fine arts schools of Lisbon and Porto, Norwich Fine Arts in the UK and the School of the Art Institute of Chicago.

Ceramics is the centre of the work, and tile art is a specialty, including tile panels for Lisbon's Alvalade metro station and for gardens at the Sakai Cultural Center in Japan. For Serax Silva has made pottery, lighting, glassware and candle holders, among them the Look At Me and Cosas Lindas collections.
On Formground Bela Silva is credited on {count} pieces shown through Serax, among them planters, table lamps, vases, bowls and floor lamps.
facts: Planters, table lamps, vases, bowls, floor lamps (as shown on Formground)

designers:muller-van-severen.name: Muller Van Severen
paragraphs: Muller Van Severen is a Belgian design studio founded in early spring 2011 by Fien Muller and Hannes Van Severen. Its studio and showroom are in Evergem, Belgium.

The studio makes sculptural furniture and lighting, plus rugs, shelves and limited editions, in materials that include marble, aluminium, brass, lacquer, ceramic and leather. Its own collections are handmade by small-scale fabricators, and it designs for brands such as Hay, Zanotta and Kvadrat. Work has been shown at Galerie Kreo and Tim Van Laere Gallery.
On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through BD Barcelona and Galerie Kreo, among them sofas, mirrors, ladders and cabinets.
facts: Sofas, mirrors, ladders, cabinets (as shown on Formground)

designers:patricia-urquiola.name: Patricia Urquiola
paragraphs: Patricia Urquiola is a Spanish architect and designer, born in Oviedo in 1961. She studied architecture in Madrid and graduated from the Politecnico di Milano in 1989 under Achille Castiglioni, then worked with Vico Magistretti and led design at Lissoni Associati.

Studio Urquiola was founded in Milan in 2001 and covers product design, architecture, art direction and strategy consulting, from hotels and retail spaces to installations. She has been art director of Cassina since 2015.
On Formground Patricia Urquiola is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them pans, cutlery sets and salad sets.
facts: Pans, cutlery sets, salad sets, grill pans (as shown on Formground)

designers:philippe-starck.name: Philippe Starck
paragraphs: Philippe Starck is a French designer and architect, born in Paris in 1949, who trained at the École Nissim de Camondo. He opened his first company in 1968, making inflatable objects, and later worked as art director for Pierre Cardin and designed interiors for President Mitterrand.

His work spans interiors, architecture, furniture, household objects, lighting and technology products. It includes the Juicy Salif citrus squeezer for Alessi, the Louis Ghost chair for Kartell, the Asahi Beer Hall in Tokyo and the Royalton Hotel in New York.
On Formground Philippe Starck is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi and Baleri Italia, among them bookcases, armchairs, stackable chairs and kitchen stools.
facts: Bookcases, armchairs, stackable chairs, kitchen stools (as shown on Formground)
sources: Lex.dk: Philippe Starck (early career, Cardin, Mitterrand)

designers:benny-frandsen.name: Benny Frandsen
paragraphs: Benny Frandsen (1941-2021) was a Danish engineer and lighting designer who founded the lamp company Frandsen in Skanderborg, Denmark. He moved its production to a factory there in 1972.

He is best known for the Ball lamp, a round wall light fixed with a magnet that has been in production for over 50 years and is now also made as a pendant, floor lamp, table lamp and spotlight. After the company was sold in 1993 he bought it back in 1996 and renamed it Frandsen Lighting. He also co-founded the Danish lighting association Dansk Belysningsforening.
On Formground Benny Frandsen is credited on {count} pieces shown through Frandsen, among them pendants, table lamps, wall lamps and floor lamps.
facts: Pendants, table lamps, wall lamps, floor lamps (as shown on Formground)

designers:oscar-tusquets.name: Oscar Tusquets
paragraphs: Òscar Tusquets Blanca is a Spanish architect, designer and painter, born in Barcelona in 1941. He graduated from the Polytechnic University of Catalonia in 1965 and in 1964 co-founded the architecture office Studio PER with Josep Bonet, Cristian Cirici and Lluís Clotet.

His architecture includes the Alfredo Kraus Auditorium in Las Palmas and the restoration and extension of the Palau de la Música Catalana, and he has designed furniture and objects such as the Simplex chair. His own site also presents his drawings, paintings and art editions, and the Fundación OTB.
On Formground Oscar Tusquets is credited on {count} pieces shown through BD Barcelona, among them chairs, dining tables and side tables.
facts: Chairs, dining tables, side tables, tables (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Òscar Tusquets (birth, training, Studio PER)

designers:claesson-koivisto-rune.name: Claesson Koivisto Rune
paragraphs: Claesson Koivisto Rune is a Swedish architecture and design studio founded in 1995 in Stockholm by Mårten Claesson, Eero Koivisto and Ola Rune, who met as students at Konstfack in 1992.

The studio works on private villas, hotels, furniture, lighting, jewellery and cement tiles, with equal weight on architecture and design. Projects include Nobis Hotel Stockholm, and manufacturers it has designed for include Wästberg, Tacchini, Paola Lenti and Iittala. For Wästberg it has designed the Bell Suspended and Cone pendant lights.
On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Wästberg, Baleri Italia and WonderGlass, among them suspension lamps, armchairs, sectional sofas and round dining tables.
facts: Suspension lamps, armchairs, sectional sofas, round dining tables, lighting (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Claesson Koivisto Rune (founders, 1995, work areas)

designers:doshi-levien.name: Doshi Levien
paragraphs: Doshi Levien is a London design studio founded in 2000 by Nipa Doshi and Jonathan Levien, who met while studying at the Royal College of Art. Doshi grew up in India, and Levien trained as a cabinetmaker.

The studio's work centres on industrial design, colour, culture and making, and draws on design traditions from around the world. Projects include the Quilton modular sofa and the Dori textile collection for HAY, and the Cala armchair for Kettal. The studio is at Columbia Road in east London.
On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them consoles, mirrors, coffee tables and cabinets.
facts: Consoles, mirrors, coffee tables, cabinets (as shown on Formground)

designers:front.name: Front
paragraphs: Front is a Swedish design studio in Stockholm, formed by Sofia Lagerkvist and Anna Lindgren. They collaborate on every project from first idea to finished product, and their objects often tell a story about the design process, the material or conventions in the field. In some projects they have handed part of the making to animals, computers or machines. Their work is represented at MoMA, the Victoria and Albert Museum, M+, Nationalmuseum, Vitra Design Museum and Centre Pompidou, and Seven Stories About Mirrors, a collection of mirrors, premiered at Galerie Kreo in 2021.
On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them mirrors, sideboards, ladders, vases and side tables.
facts: Mirrors, sideboards, ladders, vases, side tables (as shown on Formground)
sources: Galerie kreo: Front, Design Parade Villa Noailles (Seven Stories About Mirrors, 2021)

designers:main.name: Main
paragraphs: Main is a Swedish design duo made up of Elin Rahnberg and Martin Berling, who are also active as entrepreneurs, boatbuilders and retail interior designers. The duo made its debut on the Swedish design scene in 2018 with Bond, a modular shelving system for Fogia that is assembled by hand without tools. Bond was named Furniture of the Year by the magazine Residence.
On Formground Main is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fogia, among them shelving.

designers:pierre-sindre.name: Pierre Sindre
paragraphs: Pierre Sindre is a Swedish designer and interior architect, born in 1974 in Bankeryd and educated at the University of Arts, Craft and Design. He designs furniture for public spaces and works with Swedish furniture makers, most of them in Småland. His Day chair for Gärsnäs has a decorative strap between back and seat that also makes the upholstery removable. In 2022 he received the Bruno Mathsson Prize, marked by an exhibition at Vandalorum. His own site presents furniture and interior projects.
On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Gärsnäs and Källemo, among them chairs, armchairs, tables, sofas and footstools.
facts: Chairs, armchairs, tables, sofas, footstools (as shown on Formground)
sources: Vandalorum: Pierre Sindre, Bruno Mathsson Prize 2022 (birth, education, studio)

designers:antoni-arola.name: Antoni Arola
paragraphs: Antoni Arola is a designer based in Barcelona, where his studio is on Lope de Vega street. His practice is built around light, natural and artificial, and how it interacts with space, with colour as another constant. He combines artistic work with commercial projects and teaching, and his studio journal records work on the installation Canopée for LLUM BCN and classes for the Master in Lighting Design at the Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya. His site also lists awards, talks and interviews.
On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Vibia, among them pendants, ceiling lamps, table lamps and wall lamps.
facts: Pendants, ceiling lamps, table lamps, wall lamps (as shown on Formground)

designers:giulio-iacchetti.name: Giulio Iacchetti
paragraphs: Giulio Iacchetti is an Italian industrial designer who has worked since 1992 for brands including Alessi, Danese, Foscarini, Magis and Moleskine. He is known for research into new kinds of objects, such as Moscardino, a biodegradable spoon and fork designed with Matteo Ragni, which won the Compasso d'Oro in 2001. In 2012 he launched Internoitaliano, a network of craft workshops that makes furniture and accessories. The Triennale di Milano held a solo exhibition of his work in 2009. His studio site lists recent projects, among them an ice bucket for Alessi from 2025.
On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them vases, baskets and bowls, ice buckets and boxes.
facts: Vases, baskets and bowls, ice buckets, boxes (as shown on Formground)

designers:ichiro-iwasaki.name: Ichiro Iwasaki
paragraphs: Ichiro Iwasaki is a Japanese designer based in Tokyo. After early work at the Sony Design Center and a brief stint in Milan, he founded Iwasaki Design Studio in Tokyo in 1995. His work ranges from tableware, wristwatches and lighting to furniture and electronic devices such as digital cameras and mobile phones, and he lectures at Tokyo University of the Arts and Tama Art University. For Vibia he designed the Closer, Tube, Flat and Pin collections.
On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Vibia, among them pendants, table lamps, ceiling lamps and wall lamps.
facts: Pendants, table lamps, ceiling lamps, wall lamps (as shown on Formground)
sources: Vibia: Ichiro Iwasaki (Closer, Tube, Flat, Pin)

designers:jordi-vilardell.name: Jordi Vilardell
paragraphs: Jordi Vilardell is a lighting designer who has designed collections for Vibia, the Spanish lighting company, including Match, Meridiano, Suite, Wind, Puck, Slim and Join. With Meritxell Vidal he made Match, a hanging lamp that lets users combine fittings into a design suited to each space, and the Halley outdoor lights. The Meridiano outdoor lamps and the Suite lamps for interiors each combine furniture and lighting in one piece. Vibia presents the pair on its designer page.
On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Vibia, among them table lamps, wall lamps, pendants and ceiling lamps.
facts: Table lamps, wall lamps, pendants, ceiling lamps (as shown on Formground)
sources: Interiors from Spain: Jordi Vilardell designs Vibia's Meridiano collection

designers:hannes-wettstein.name: Hannes Wettstein
paragraphs: Hannes Wettstein (1958 to 2008) was a Swiss designer working in Zurich. He completed an apprenticeship as a structural engineering draughtsman and then trained himself as a designer and architect. He designed the lightweight Juliette chair for Baleri Italia before turning 30, and the company's Capri armchair won the Compasso d'Oro in 1994. He also designed furniture for Cassina, Molteni, Arflex, Wittmann and Erik Jørgensen, lighting for Artemide and Oluce, watches, and interiors for Swiss embassies.
On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Baleri Italia and Fredericia, among them armchairs, sofas, stackable chairs, kitchen stools and bar stools.
facts: Armchairs, sofas, stackable chairs, kitchen stools, bar stools (as shown on Formground)
sources: Architectural Record: Hannes Wettstein, 50, Swiss Designer (2008)

designers:maurice-harris.name: Maurice Harris
paragraphs: Maurice Harris is a Los Angeles-based artist, best known as the creator of Bloom & Plume, a bespoke floral design studio in Echo Park. His clients include brands such as Louis Vuitton, Dior and Nike, and institutions such as MOCA and LACMA. His art practice has included a flower sculpture at MOCA, photography at the San Diego Art Institute and a performance piece at the Broad, and he has appeared in the television series Centerpiece. The Bloom & Plume site presents his work and shop.
On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Serax, among them vases.

designers:michael-graves.name: Michael Graves
paragraphs: Michael Graves (1934 to 2015) was an American architect and designer, born in Indianapolis. He studied architecture at the University of Cincinnati and earned a master's degree at Harvard in 1959. Alongside buildings he designed consumer products for companies including Alessi in Italy and Target and J. C. Penney in the United States; his 9093 teakettle for Alessi dates from 1985. The firm Michael Graves Architecture and Design continues at michaelgraves.com, with architecture and product projects.
On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them electric kettles, kettles and kettle accessories.
facts: Electric kettles, kettles, kettle accessories (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Michael Graves (education, career, Alessi, dates)

designers:nanna-ditzel.name: Nanna Ditzel
paragraphs: Nanna Ditzel (1923 to 2005) was a Danish designer, born in Copenhagen. She trained as a carpenter at Richards Skole and graduated from the Danish School of Arts and Crafts in 1946. Her work included furniture, jewellery, tableware and textiles, among them the Hanging Egg Chair, the Trinidad chair and the Toad stool, and she received the Lunning Prize in 1956. Fredericia has reintroduced her Trisse from 1962, now in solid oak.
On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fredericia, among them lounge chairs, dining chairs, armchairs, bar stools and stools.
facts: Lounge chairs, dining chairs, armchairs, bar stools, stools (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Nanna Ditzel (dates, training, works, Lunning Prize)
Fredericia: Trisse Collection by Nanna Ditzel

designers:robin-day.name: Robin Day
paragraphs: Robin Day (1915 to 2010) was a British furniture and industrial designer, born in High Wycombe. He studied at High Wycombe School of Art and from 1934 at the Royal College of Art. His career spanned more than seventy years and moved between furniture, interiors, exhibitions and graphics; he is known for the polypropylene stacking chair for Hille and the seating for the Royal Festival Hall. The Robin and Lucienne Day Foundation maintains an official site on his and Lucienne Day's work.
On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through &Tradition and Galerie Kreo, among them furniture accessories, outdoor dining tables, chairs, lounge chairs and side chairs.
facts: Furniture accessories, outdoor dining tables, chairs, lounge chairs, side chairs (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Robin Day (designer) (dates, training, known works)

designers:antoni-gaudi.name: Antoni Gaudí
paragraphs: Antoni Gaudí (1852 to 1926) was a Catalan architect and designer, born in Reus or Riudoms and active mainly in Barcelona. His works include the Sagrada Família, Casa Milà, Casa Batlló and Park Güell. He combined crafts such as ceramics, stained glass, wrought ironwork and carpentry, and introduced trencadís, a technique using waste ceramic pieces. The Sagrada Família site presents his life and method.
On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through BD Barcelona.
sources: Wikipedia: Antoni Gaudí (dates, works, crafts, trencadís)

designers:hugo-passos.name: Hugo Passos
paragraphs: Hugo Passos is a Portuguese designer, originally from Setúbal, who works from Copenhagen, where his office is in Nørrebro. He designs everyday objects and furniture with an interest in human scale and in designs doing what they are meant to do. He came to furniture through the work of Marcel Breuer, found in architecture books, and chose it over architecture. In 2023 Fredericia released his Gomo chair and sofa during 3daysofdesign in Copenhagen.
On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fredericia, among them sofas, side tables, armchairs, coffee tables and ottomans.
facts: Sofas, side tables, armchairs, coffee tables, ottomans (as shown on Formground)
sources: Norse Projects: Seating Arrangement, a conversation with Hugo Passos (2023)

designers:martin-azua.name: Martín Azúa
paragraphs: Martín Azúa is a designer based in Barcelona, who has taught at the Elisava school since 1995. He studied fine arts at the University of Barcelona and has designed products for companies including nanimarquina, Vibia, Roca, Kvadrat and Droog Design. For Vibia his designs include the Halo and Dots lamps. His project Casa Básica is in the collection of MoMA in New York, and in 2010 he was named Spanish designer of the year by AD.
On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Vibia, among them wall lamps, pendants, ceiling lamps and table lamps.
facts: Wall lamps, pendants, ceiling lamps, table lamps (as shown on Formground)
sources: Stylepark: Martín Azúa (address, studies, Vibia products)
Elisava: Martín Ruiz de Azúa (teaching, clients, MoMA, awards)

designers:norm-architects.name: Norm Architects
paragraphs: Norm Architects is a Copenhagen-based practice founded in 2008 by Jonas Bjerre-Poulsen and Kasper Rønn. It works across architecture, interiors, furniture and products, with a minimalist approach built on natural materials, tactility and light. For Fogia the studio designed the Embrace series, which pairs a sculptural outer shell with a soft interior, and the Koku tables, which balance solid oak with slender steel tubing. Its projects and awards are listed on the practice's website.
On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fogia, among them coffee tables, ottomans, lounge chairs and side tables.
facts: Coffee tables, ottomans, lounge chairs, side tables (as shown on Formground)

designers:philippe-malouin.name: Philippe Malouin
paragraphs: Philippe Malouin is a British-Canadian designer, born in Laval, Quebec. He studied at the University of Montreal, the École Nationale Supérieure de Création Industrielle in Paris and the Design Academy Eindhoven, set up his studio in 2008, and lives and works in London.

His portfolio covers sofas, tables, rugs, chairs, lights, art objects and installations, with clients including Flos, Zanotta, SCP and Alessi. His 2021 exhibition Steel Works used salvaged steel components found in junkyards. His site is philippemalouin.com. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Resident and Alessi, among them espresso coffee makers, armchairs, sofas and chairs.
facts: Espresso coffee makers, armchairs, sofas, chairs, storage (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Philippe Malouin (birthplace, training, Steel Works, Alessi)

designers:pool.name: Pool
paragraphs: Pool is a Paris-based studio founded by Léa Padovani and Sébastien Kieffer, who met while working for the designer Noé Duchaufour-Lawrence. The studio works across design, graphics, art direction and interior design, and designs its own furniture collection alongside work with ateliers, factories, galleries and furniture editors.

It has made products for La Chance, Petite Friture and Gallery S. Bensimon, among them the Maillet lamp in hammered copper and painted metal. On Formground Pool is credited on {count} pieces shown through CVL, among them wall lamps, pendants, floor lamps and table lamps.
facts: Wall lamps, pendants, floor lamps, table lamps (as shown on Formground)
sources: Sight Unseen: Pool at Interieur Biennale (2014)

designers:ilse-crawford.name: Ilse Crawford
paragraphs: Ilse Crawford is a British designer, born in London in 1962. She was launch editor of Elle Decoration, worked for Donna Karan from 1998, and in 2000 founded the Man and Well-Being department at the Design Academy Eindhoven.

She is the founder of Studioilse, a multidisciplinary London-based team that designs homes, public spaces, products and brand identities. The studio's site is studioilse.com. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through nanimarquina and Wästberg, among them home textiles, indoor rugs, table lamps and tapestries.
facts: Home textiles, indoor rugs, table lamps, tapestries (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Ilse Crawford (birth, career, Design Academy Eindhoven)

designers:sebastian-herkner.name: Sebastian Herkner
paragraphs: Sebastian Herkner is a German designer, born in 1981. He studied product design at the HfG Offenbach and worked briefly for Stella McCartney in London. He founded his own design studio in Offenbach am Main in 2006 and has taught at the HfG Offenbach as a visiting lecturer since 2007.

He designs products for international manufacturers and works on interiors, exhibitions and museum projects; his prizes include the 2011 German Design Award in the Newcomer category. His studio's site is sebastianherkner.com. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through &Tradition and Vibia, among them mirrors, wall lamps, table lamps, pendants and side tables.
facts: Mirrors, wall lamps, table lamps, pendants, side tables (as shown on Formground)

designers:simon-james.name: Simon James
paragraphs: Simon James is a New Zealand furniture designer who studied Spatial Design at AUT. He set up Simon James Design around 2001 to sell his own furniture and to introduce international furniture and lighting to New Zealand, and in 2011 co-founded the export brand Resident with Scott Bridgens.

His furniture is built on simplicity, honest materials and lasting craftsmanship, and his own designs are shown at the studio's site, simonjames.co.nz, alongside the work of others. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Resident, among them chairs, stools and sofas.
facts: Chairs, seating, stools, sofas (as shown on Formground)
sources: I Love Ugly: Simon James talks to I Love Ugly (2015)

designers:pietro-leemann.name: Pietro Leemann
paragraphs: Pietro Leemann is a Michelin-starred chef who, with a group of colleagues, founded the vegetarian restaurant Joia in Milan in 1989.

For Alessi's Convivio range, developed with David Chipperfield and launched in October 2023, he took part in analysing vegetarian cooking so that pots, pans and utensils were matched in size, type and technology and suited to vegetables and pulses. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them pots, lids, grill pans, pans and kitchen cutlery.
facts: Pots, lids, grill pans, pans, kitchen cutlery (as shown on Formground)
sources: David Chipperfield Architects: Convivio pots and pans

designers:john-kandell.name: John Kandell
paragraphs: John Kandell is a furniture designer whose chairs and shelves are produced by the Swedish manufacturer Källemo. The Barnbarn chair was designed in 1966 and put into production in 1985, in solid mahogany or walnut with leather seat and armrests.

Camilla (1982), a beech chair, was printed on Swedish stamps in 2005, and Schablon followed in 1987. The Pilaster shelf (1989) grew from the idea of stacking books horizontally, and was communicated to Källemo's founder by phone without a drawing. On Formground Kandell is credited on {count} pieces shown through Källemo, among them chairs, shelves and armchairs.
facts: Chairs, armchairs, shelves (as shown on Formground)

designers:nao-tamura.name: Nao Tamura
paragraphs: Nao Tamura is a designer based in New York who grew up in Tokyo and studied at Parsons School of Design. Her work covers furniture, lighting, installations, public space and space design, from the Origata furniture for PORRO to the Flow[T] and Fluid lighting for WonderGlass.

She has presented room-scale installations at Palais de Tokyo and the Kyoto City KYOCERA Museum of Art, and Origata received a Compasso d'Oro Honourable Mention. Her site is naotamura.com. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through WonderGlass and nanimarquina, among them lighting, objects and indoor rugs.
facts: Lighting, objects, indoor rugs (as shown on Formground)

designers:nendo.name: Nendo
paragraphs: Nendo is a Japanese design firm founded in 2002 by Oki Sato, who graduated with a master's degree in architecture from Waseda University that year. Its first office was in Tokyo and a second opened in Milan in 2005. The name is the Japanese word for clay.

The firm works globally with a large number of brands, and held its first exhibition, streeterior, in Milan and Tokyo in 2003. Its site is nendo.jp. On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through WonderGlass, Alessi and &Tradition, among them lighting, objects, electric kettles, toasters and electric citrus squeezers.
facts: Lighting, objects, electric kettles, toasters, electric citrus squeezers (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Nendo (design firm) (founding, offices, first exhibition)

designers:nika-zupanc.name: Nika Zupanc
paragraphs: Nika Zupanc is a Slovenian industrial designer, born in Ljubljana in 1974, who works in furniture, product and interior design. She graduated from the Ljubljana Academy of Fine Arts and Design in 2000, showed at SaloneSatellite at the Milan Furniture Fair soon afterwards, and set up her own studio in 2008. She lives and works in London.

Her designs have been produced by companies including Alessi, Moooi, Qeeboo, Driade and Natuzzi, and a monograph, Nika Zupanc: Breaking the Rules, was published by Rizzoli in 2022. Her site is nikazupanc.com. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi and Ghidini 1961, among them chairs, candlesticks and Christmas table accessories.
facts: Baskets and centrepieces, chairs, Christmas tree ornaments, table accessories, candlesticks (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Nika Zupanc (birth, training, studio, clients)

designers:toni-rie.name: Toni Rie
paragraphs: Toni Rie is a lighting designer who has worked with the lighting company Frandsen since 2013. Her designs range from strong geometric, modern forms to more organic and atmospheric ones.

She designed the Lyss series, a family of wall, pendant, floor and table lamps built on a cylindrical top and a conical shade, and the Butterfly family, whose lamps combine half domes, with perforations in the top dome that let light diffuse upwards. On Formground Toni Rie is credited on {count} pieces shown through Frandsen, among them table lamps, floor lamps, wall lamps and pendants.
facts: Table lamps, floor lamps, wall lamps, pendants (as shown on Formground)

designers:xucla.name: Xuclà
paragraphs: Josep Lluís Xuclà is a designer born in Barcelona in 1956 and based in the city. He founded a studio under his own name that works on interior design, lighting and furniture, and he enrolled at Barcelona's Llotja school of design and art in the 1970s.

His product design rests on minimalism and simple shapes. For Vibia he has designed the Empty, Set, Break and Palo Alto collections, and Marset lists its High Line lamp among his designs. On Formground Xuclà is credited on {count} pieces shown through Vibia, among them table lamps, wall lamps and ceiling lamps.
facts: Table lamps, wall lamps, ceiling lamps (as shown on Formground)
sources: Marset: Josep Lluís Xuclà (born Barcelona 1956, studio, High Line)

designers:achille-castiglioni.name: Achille Castiglioni
paragraphs: Achille Castiglioni (1918–2002) was an Italian architect and designer born in Milan. He graduated in architecture from the Politecnico di Milano in 1944, joined the practice his brothers Livio and Pier Giacomo had started, and worked with Pier Giacomo as a team until 1968. He later taught as a professor at the Politecnico di Milano.

Together with Pier Giacomo he designed the Arco floor lamp for Flos and the Mezzadro and Sella stools for Zanotta, and he designed the Record wristwatch for Alessi. His archive is kept by the Achille Castiglioni Foundation in his Milan studio museum. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them wall clocks and fruit bowls.
facts: Wall clocks, fruit bowls (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Achille Castiglioni (training, career, teaching, archive)

designers:angelo-mangiarotti.name: Angelo Mangiarotti
paragraphs: Angelo Mangiarotti (1921–2012) was an Italian architect and industrial designer, born and based in Milan. He graduated from the Politecnico di Milano in 1948, was a visiting professor at the Illinois Institute of Technology in 1953, and in 1989 opened an architectural practice in Tokyo.

Besides industrial buildings and railway stations, he designed the Lesbo and Saffo lamps for Artemide and Carrara marble tables held together by gravity joints, among them Eros from 1971. In 1994 he received the Compasso d'Oro for lifetime achievement. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Baleri Italia and Galerie Kreo, among them cups, dining tables, side tables and consoles.
facts: Cups, dining tables, central tables, side tables, consoles (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Angelo Mangiarotti (training, practice, works, award)

designers:hans-j-wegner.name: Hans J. Wegner
paragraphs: Hans J. Wegner (1914–2007) was a Danish furniture designer, born in Tønder as the son of a cobbler. He trained as a cabinetmaker, studied at the School of Arts and Crafts in Copenhagen, and in the late 1930s and early 1940s designed the furnishings for Aarhus City Hall, a building by Arne Jacobsen and Erik Møller.

Wegner is known above all for chairs, which he designed in the hundreds, and his CH24 Wishbone Chair has been in continuous production since 1950. His work shows a close attention to wood and joinery. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fredericia, among them lounge chairs, coffee tables, ottomans and stools.
facts: Lounge chairs, coffee tables, ottomans, stools (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Hans Wegner (birth, training, Aarhus City Hall)
Carl Hansen & Søn: Hans J. Wegner (Wishbone Chair, craft)

designers:john-pawson.name: John Pawson
paragraphs: John Pawson is a British architectural designer, born in Halifax in 1949, whose work is known for its minimalist approach. He studied at the Architectural Association School of Architecture in London and set up his own practice in 1981.

Alongside buildings, his studio's site lists furniture, lighting, tapware, homeware and books. His lighting includes Berg for WonderGlass and the w223 Pawson table lamp for Wästberg. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through WonderGlass and Wästberg, among them lighting, table lamps, coffee tables, side tables and pendants.
facts: Lighting, table lamps, coffee tables, side tables, pendants (as shown on Formground)
sources: John Pawson: Design (product and collaboration list)
Wikipedia: John Pawson (birth, training, practice founded 1981)

designers:lluis-clotet.name: Lluís Clotet
paragraphs: Lluís Clotet is a Spanish architect and designer, born in Barcelona in 1941. He graduated from the Barcelona School of Architecture in 1965, taught there, and in 1964 founded Studio PER with Pep Bonet, Cristian Cirici and Oscar Tusquets. He is also a founder of BD Ediciones, a publisher specialising in design.

With Tusquets he worked on many projects, among them designs for BD Barcelona such as Cornisa and the 3-4-5 mailbox, until 1983. From 1984 to 2008 he worked in partnership with Ignacio Paricio. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi and BD Barcelona, among them serving plates.

designers:monica-forster.name: Monica Förster
paragraphs: Monica Förster is a designer who founded and leads Monica Förster Design Studio in Stockholm. The studio describes its approach as poetic design that joins form, function and emotion, and it works on products and spaces.

It works with brands including Alessi, Artifort, Georg Jensen, Fredericia, Offecct, Poltrona Frau, Svenskt Tenn, Tacchini and Zanotta. The rug collection I Inherited a Forest, made with Ogeborg, received the Swedish Utmärkt Svensk Form award. On Formground Monica Förster is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fogia and Fredericia, among them sofas, side tables, lounge chairs and coffee tables.
facts: Sofas, side tables, lounge chairs, coffee tables (as shown on Formground)
sources: Monica Förster Design Studio: The Studio

designers:odo-fioravanti.name: Odo Fioravanti
paragraphs: Odo Fioravanti is an industrial designer who studied industrial design at the Design Department of the Politecnico di Milano. He founded Odo Fioravanti Design Studio, has taught at schools including the Politecnico di Milano, Domus Academy and HEAD Genève, and also works with graphic and exhibition design.

In 2010 the Triennale Design Museum in Milan held a solo exhibition of his work, and in 2011 he won the Compasso d'Oro with the Frida wooden chair for Pedrali. For Baleri Italia he designed the InBallo series. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Baleri Italia, among them armchairs, sofas and modular units.
facts: Armchairs, sofas, modular units (as shown on Formground)

designers:lievore-altherr-molina.name: Lievore Altherr Molina
paragraphs: Lievore Altherr Molina was a design studio in Barcelona. Jeannette Altherr was a founding partner from 1990 to 2015, after which the practice continued as Lievore Altherr until 2019. Delphine Désile worked there as a senior designer from 1999, and Dennis Park joined in 2006.

In 2019 Altherr, Désile and Park co-founded the Barcelona studio Altherr Désile Park, which works with companies such as Arper, Poltrona Frau and Vibia. On Formground Lievore Altherr Molina is credited on {count} pieces shown through Vibia, among them table lamps, pendants and wall lamps.
facts: Table lamps, pendants, wall lamps (as shown on Formground)
sources: Altherr Désile Park: About (partners' histories at Lievore Altherr Molina)

designers:meike-harde.name: Meike Harde
paragraphs: Studio Meike Harde is a product design studio in Cologne, Germany, working on upholstery, lighting and other furniture. Meike Harde studied product design at HBK Saar from 2006 to 2011, interned at Studio Benjamin Hubert in London in 2012 and has run the studio since 2013.

The studio describes a particular knowledge of textiles and works for brands including Vibia, Pode, Woud, Ligne Roset and Bolia. On Formground Meike Harde is credited on {count} pieces shown through Pode and Vibia, among them pendants, table lamps, sofas, corner sofas and tables.
facts: Pendants, table lamps, sofas, corner sofas, tables (as shown on Formground)

designers:ariadna-miquel.name: Ariadna Miquel
paragraphs: Ariadna Miquel is a designer who graduated in industrial design from the Elisava Barcelona School of Design and received the ADI-FAD Award in 2002 for her final year project. After working with Martín Azúa and Emiliana Design Studio in 2003, she joined the design team at nanimarquina and stayed until 2016.

Her work is shaped by an interest in textiles and production techniques, with a focus on texture and the application of colour. The Bicicleta rug, co-designed with and for nanimarquina, is in the permanent collection of the Design Museum of Barcelona. On Formground Ariadna Miquel is credited on {count} pieces shown through nanimarquina, among them indoor rugs.

designers:michael-anastassiades.name: Michael Anastassiades
paragraphs: Michael Anastassiades is a Cypriot-born, London-based designer whose practice covers product, spatial interventions and experimental works. He trained as a civil engineer at Imperial College London and took a master's degree in industrial design at the Royal College of Art before founding his studio in London in 1994.

The studio has conceived lights, furniture and objects and has worked with manufacturers including Flos, B&B Italia, Herman Miller and Cassina. Its Flos lights include Arrangements, Captain Flint and Coordinates. On Formground Anastassiades is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them candles, containers, fragrance diffusers and espresso coffee makers.
facts: Candles, containers, fragrance diffusers, espresso coffee makers, kitchen accessories (as shown on Formground)

designers:valerio-sommella.name: Valerio Sommella
paragraphs: Valerio Sommella is an Italian industrial designer based in Milan, trained at the Politecnico di Milano. He founded Valerio Sommella Studio, which develops furniture, lighting, consumer electronics, tableware and limited edition objects.

The studio's site lists work for brands including Alessi, Falmec, Nemo Lighting, Moooi, Ethimo and Tidelli, among them the Octave glassware collection for Ichendorf and the Jasmine outdoor seating for Tidelli, designed with Simone Bonanni. On Formground Valerio Sommella is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them serving cutlery, bottle openers and graters.
facts: Serving cutlery, bottle openers, graters (as shown on Formground)

designers:virgil-abloh.name: Virgil Abloh
paragraphs: Virgil Abloh (1980–2021) was an American artist, architect, art director and fashion designer, born in Rockford, Illinois. He studied civil engineering at the University of Wisconsin–Madison and took a master's degree in architecture at the Illinois Institute of Technology. He founded Off-White, and was artistic director of Louis Vuitton menswear from 2018 to 2021.

In furniture he collaborated with Vitra on the Spin-off collection and showed the efflorescence collection, designed at his research studio Alaska Alaska, at Galerie kreo in 2020, his first show at a contemporary design gallery. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo and Alessi, among them a ladder.
sources: Wikipedia: Virgil Abloh (birth, training, Off-White, Louis Vuitton)

designers:santi-moix.name: Santi Moix
paragraphs: Santi Moix is an artist born in Barcelona in 1960. He has lived in New York since 1986 and keeps studios in Brooklyn and Barcelona. His work spans painting, sculpture, drawing, ceramics, mural painting and book illustration, mixing figuration with abstraction.

For nanimarquina he made the Flora rug collection, three hand-tufted designs (Promenade, Backyard and Bloom) built on his imagery of flowers from bud to decay. On Formground Santi Moix is credited on {count} pieces shown through nanimarquina, among them indoor rugs.

designers:tim-rundle.name: Tim Rundle
paragraphs: Tim Rundle is a New Zealand-born industrial designer, now based in London. He runs Tim Rundle Studio, working across furniture, lighting, consumer products and transport.
