Earlier jobs included Priestmangoode, Tom Dixon and Conran + Partners, and he is a tutor on the Royal College of Art's Design Products MA.

He has designed the Bloom pendant and the Radio Chair for Resident, and chairs and tables for the Australian brand SP01. On Formground Tim Rundle is credited on {count} pieces shown through Resident, among them pendant lamps, chairs, stools, floor lamps and table lamps.
facts: Pendant lamps, chairs, stools, floor lamps, table lamps (as shown on Formground)
sources: Indesign Live: Tim Rundle and SP01
Dezeen: Resident at 3 Days of Design (Radio Chair)

designers:toyo-ito.name: Toyo Ito
paragraphs: Toyo Ito is a Japanese architect born in 1941 in Keijo, now Seoul. He graduated in architecture from the University of Tokyo in 1965 and founded his Tokyo practice in 1971 as Urbot, renamed Toyo Ito & Associates in 1979. Among his buildings are the Sendai Mediatheque and the 2002 Serpentine Gallery Pavilion.

For Alessi he designed the KU porcelain tableware in 2006 and the MU stainless steel cutlery, whose handles end in a hexagonal profile and which was shown in 2013. On Formground Toyo Ito is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them a cutlery set, cups, salad serving bowls and serving plates.
facts: Cutlery set, cups, salad serving bowls, serving plates (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Toyo Ito (birth, training, practice, buildings)
Dezeen: MU cutlery by Toyo Ito for Alessi

designers:abi-alice.name: Abi Alice
paragraphs: Abi Alice is an artist and designer based in London. Born in Sydney, Abi Alice completed a bachelor's degree in 1996 and a master's in fine art in 2007 at the College of Fine Arts, University of New South Wales. The work starts from mathematics and geometry, with compositions drawn on grid paper that become paintings and sometimes three-dimensional objects.

Four pieces for Alessi, Resonance (2006), Harmonic and Small Resonance (2008) and Pianissimo (2009), turn these drawings into cut, folded and curved stainless steel. On Formground Abi Alice is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them baskets.
sources: Victoria and Albert Museum: Harmonic maquette (E.634-2015)

designers:ann-demeulemeester.name: Ann Demeulemeester
paragraphs: Ann Demeulemeester is a Belgian designer, born in Waregem in 1959, who studied fashion design at the Royal Academy of Fine Arts in Antwerp. She launched her fashion label in 1985 and is counted among the Antwerp Six, a group of Belgian designers from the 1980s.

Since 2019 she has worked with Serax on porcelain, cutlery and glassware, followed by lighting and, in 2022, a furniture range of stools, chairs, tables, consoles and sofas. On Formground Ann Demeulemeester is credited on {count} pieces shown through Serax, among them tables.

designers:atelier-o.name: Atelier Oï
paragraphs: Atelier Oï is a Swiss design studio, founded in 1991 in La Neuveville by Aurel Aebi, Armand Louis and Patrick Reymond. Its name comes from the Russian word troïka, a team of three. The studio works across architecture, interior design, product design and scenography, and has collaborated with Louis Vuitton and Foscarini.

With WonderGlass it made Collection Gaïa, five glass works including Marea, Éos, Parhelia, Séléné and Aura, first shown from its La Neuveville headquarters. On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through WonderGlass, among them lighting.
sources: WonderGlass: Marea by atelier oï (studio background)
Dezeen: Atelier Oï previews its glass collection

designers:begum-cana-ozgur.name: Begüm Cana Özgür
paragraphs: Begüm Cana Özgür, who goes by Cana, is a product and textile designer based in Istanbul and New York. After studying interior architecture at Bilkent University she took a master's in 3D design at Cranbrook Academy of Art, where she learned weaving, and returned to Istanbul to start her studio in 2014.

She works with weavers in Anatolia, and her first flat-weave rug collection, SHADE, was relaunched by nanimarquina in 2017. On Formground Begüm Cana Özgür is credited on {count} pieces shown through nanimarquina, among them indoor and outdoor rugs and poufs.
facts: Indoor and outdoor rugs, indoor and outdoor poufs (as shown on Formground)
sources: Global Thinkers Forum: Begüm Cânâ Özgür
Revival Rugs: an interview with Begüm Cana Özgür

designers:claire-vos.name: Claire Vos
paragraphs: Claire Vos is a textile designer based in the Netherlands. She studied at the Design Academy Eindhoven and trained in Italy and Indonesia. In 1999 she and designer Roderick Vos started Studio Roderick Vos in Heusden Vesting, designing lighting, textiles, accessories and furniture for international brands.

Her work re-interprets traditional techniques and forms, and includes the Bead and Liquid Layers rugs for Moooi Carpets. On Formground Claire Vos is credited on {count} pieces shown through Pode, among them accessories.

designers:david-regestam.name: David Regestam
paragraphs: David Regestam is a Swedish architect and designer, born in 1980, who studied design at the University of Gothenburg and interior architecture and furniture design at the University College of Arts, Crafts and Design in Stockholm. Since graduating in 2007 the work has combined architecture, interiors and furniture, at times in Japan with Junichi Tokuda.

He designed the Steelo ottoman (2012) for Karl Andersson & Söner and the Viva chair for Gärsnäs, shown at Salone del Mobile in 2019, as well as Gärsnäs's Tak and Kolonn tables. On Formground David Regestam is credited on {count} pieces shown through Gärsnäs, among them lighting, tables and chairs.
facts: Lighting, tables, chairs (as shown on Formground)

designers:enrico-baleri.name: Enrico Baleri
paragraphs: Enrico Baleri was an Italian designer and entrepreneur, born in 1942 in Albino near Bergamo. In 1965, on Dino Gavina's suggestion, he opened a furniture showroom in Bergamo. He was a founding member of the Pluri research group in Milan in 1968 and set up Alias in 1979, serving as its art director until 1983.

He designed furniture, lighting and objects for Gavina, Flos, Knoll and Alias, and in 1984 founded Baleri Italia with Marilisa Decimo. Interni magazine reported his death at the age of 83 in 2025. On Formground Enrico Baleri is credited on {count} pieces shown through Baleri Italia, among them seats and footrests.
facts: Seats and footrests (as shown on Formground)
sources: Interni: Enrico Baleri, not just design

designers:doriana-e-massimiliano-fuksas.name: Doriana e Massimiliano Fuksas
paragraphs: Doriana and Massimiliano Fuksas lead Studio Fuksas, an international architecture practice with offices in Rome, Paris and Shenzhen. Massimiliano Fuksas, born in Rome in 1944, opened his first office in Rome in 1967; Doriana Fuksas is his partner in the studio. The practice reports more than 600 projects and a staff of about 170.

Alongside buildings, the studio has designed product collections, among them the Colombina cutlery and tableware for Alessi. On Formground Doriana e Massimiliano Fuksas are credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them a cutlery set, trays and oyster knives.
facts: Cutlery set, trays, oyster knives (as shown on Formground)

designers:foster-partners-industrial-des.name: Foster + Partners Industrial Design
paragraphs: Foster + Partners Industrial Design is the product design side of Foster + Partners, the British architecture firm founded in 1967 by Norman Foster and headquartered in London. The firm's practice spans architecture, engineering and industrial design.

Wästberg lists the group among the designers whose lighting it makes, alongside David Chipperfield, John Pawson, Inga Sempé and others. On Formground Foster + Partners Industrial Design is credited on {count} pieces shown through Wästberg, among them suspension, ceiling, semi-recessed and track lamps.
facts: Suspension, ceiling, semi-recessed and track lamps (as shown on Formground)

designers:frederic-gooris.name: Frédéric Gooris
paragraphs: Frédéric Gooris is a Belgian industrial designer, born in Leuven in 1974. He graduated as an engineer from Hogeschool Antwerpen in 1998, took a master's in design at Domus Academy in Milan, and spent five years working with Philippe Starck and Stefano Giovannoni. He founded Studio Gooris in Milan in 2004 and moved to Hong Kong in 2010.

For Alessi he designed the Virgula Divina bottle opener and the Objets-Bijoux family, which includes the Pip key ring and the Jumbo and Minou bag hooks. On Formground Frédéric Gooris is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them bottle openers.
facts: Bottle openers and small accessories (as shown on Formground)

designers:jeff-miller.name: Jeff Miller
paragraphs: Jeff Miller is an American industrial designer who works in consumer products, electronics, furniture and interiors. He studied industrial design at Carnegie Mellon University, was vice president of design at ECCO Design in New York, and in 2011 joined Poppin as vice president of design. He has also run his own New York practice, with clients including Bosch, Herman Miller and Lenovo.

For Baleri Italia he designed the Bentz tables, the Flipt armchair, the Obo modular unit and the Fratino dining table. On Formground Jeff Miller is credited on {count} pieces shown through Baleri Italia.
facts: Armchair/chaise longue, modular unit, dining and low tables (as shown on Formground)

designers:kristiina-lassus.name: Kristiina Lassus
paragraphs: Kristiina Lassus is a Finnish product designer and interior architect, born in Helsinki in 1966. She earned master's degrees in design leadership (1992) and in interior architecture and furniture design (1995) at the University of Industrial Arts Helsinki, and has lived in Italy since 1997.

She worked as design manager at Alessi from 1998 to 2004 and founded Kristiina Lassus Studio in Milan in 2003. Her Alessi designs include the Tibidabo serving cutlery and the Tau tray. On Formground Kristiina Lassus is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them serving cutlery, trays, creamers and sugar bowls.
facts: Serving cutlery, trays, creamers, sugar bowls (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Kristiina Lassus (training, Alessi role, studio)

designers:palomba-serafini-associati.name: Palomba Serafini Associati
paragraphs: Palomba Serafini Associati is an architecture and design studio founded in Milan in 1994 by Ludovica Serafini and Roberto Palomba. The studio works on architecture and interiors as well as products, and combines a contemporary view of users' needs with knowledge of the historical roots of design.

Its project list includes the BeBop chair for Kartell, the Lama and Noli pieces for Zanotta, the Birdie lamp for Foscarini and collections for Ideal Standard. On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Vibia, among them table lamps and pendants.
facts: Table lamps, pendants (as shown on Formground)

designers:pauline-deltour.name: Pauline Deltour
paragraphs: Pauline Deltour is a French designer, born in 1983 in Landerneau, Brittany. She graduated in industrial design from ENSAD in Paris in 2007 and worked from 2006 in Konstantin Grcic's Munich studio. In 2010 she opened her own studio in Paris and launched A Tempo, her first collection, for Alessi.

Later work includes the Signal collection for the French lighting maker CVL Luminaires, the Patio garden furniture for Tolix and rugs for Hem. On Formground Pauline Deltour is credited on {count} pieces shown through CVL and Alessi, among them wall lamps, pendants and floor lamps.
facts: Wall lamps, pendants, floor lamps and tableware accessories (as shown on Formground)

designers:cecilie-manz.name: Cecilie Manz
paragraphs: Cecilie Manz is a Danish designer who studied at the Danish Design School in Copenhagen and at the Finnish School of Art and Design in Helsinki, graduating in 1997. She founded her studio, Manz Lab, in Copenhagen in 1998 and still works there.

Her projects cover furniture, tableware, lighting and audio products, including the Mikado table, the Caravaggio lamp for Lightyears and the Moky chair from 2016. Drawings are made on paper and shapes are developed in a workshop in the studio's basement. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fredericia, among them lounge chairs, dining chairs and tables.
facts: Lounge chairs, dining chairs, dining and coffee tables (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Cecilie Manz (training, 1998 studio, selected designs)
Fritz Hansen: In the studio with Cecilie Manz (working method)

designers:campana-brothers.name: Campana Brothers
paragraphs: Campana Brothers are Humberto Campana (born 1953) and Fernando Campana (1961-2022), who co-founded Estudio Campana in São Paulo, Brazil, in 1984. The studio makes furniture and objects from an unusually wide range of materials, including aluminium, wood, leather, rope and upcycled packaging.

Early pieces include the Vermelha chair (1993) and the Favela chair (1998), and in 1998 the studio took part in a project with Ingo Maurer curated for the Museum of Modern Art in New York. On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Ghidini 1961, among them lamps, sculptures and vases.
facts: Lamps, sculptures, vases (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Campana brothers (founding, birth and death years, early pieces)

designers:ernest-race.name: Ernest Race
paragraphs: Ernest Race (1913-1964) was an English furniture designer who studied interior design at the Bartlett School of Architecture in London and began his career at the lighting manufacturer Troughton & Young. In 1945 he founded Race Furniture.

He is best known for post-war seating in aluminium and laminated wood, including the BA3 chair of 1945 and the Antelope, designed for the 1951 Festival of Britain. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them armchairs, coffee tables, shelving and cabinets.
facts: Armchairs, coffee tables, shelving, cabinets (as shown on Formground)

designers:big-game.name: Big-Game
paragraphs: Big-Game is a design studio in Lausanne, Switzerland, founded in 2004 by Grégoire Jeanmonod, Elric Petit and Augustin Scott de Martinville, who met at ECAL, the art and design school in Lausanne.

The studio works on products and furniture, and also on identities, art direction, interiors, scenography and exhibitions. A 2008 Dezeen overview names collections such as Heritage in Progress and Plus Is More, and collaborators including Ligne Roset and Galerie Kreo. On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo and Alessi.

designers:studiopluz.name: Studiopluz
paragraphs: Studiopluz is a multidisciplinary studio in London founded by the artist Simone Zecubi, who previously worked at Arnaldo Pomodoro Studio in Milan and at Karl Lagerfeld Studio. The studio blends art and design.

Its consultancy work covers art direction, graphic and visual design and fashion design, with a focus on accessory lines. WonderGlass lists the studio among its creatives, with pieces such as the Minosse chair and table, Kimera, Echoes and Dondolo. On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through WonderGlass, among them objects, lighting and tables.
facts: Objects, lighting, tables (as shown on Formground)

designers:andre-monpoix.name: André Monpoix
paragraphs: André Monpoix (1925-1976) was a furniture designer who graduated from the École des Arts Décoratifs in 1949, opened his own agency in 1952 and worked with Meubles TV from 1955. He received a gold medal at the 1958 Brussels World Fair.

In 1967 he received several projects from Mobilier national, among them Dialogue, a modular seating system for the Ministry of Health and Social Affairs that Source Édition reissued with Mobilier national. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Source Édition, among them lounge chairs and sofas.
facts: Lounge chairs, sofas (as shown on Formground)

designers:anton-bjorsing.name: Anton Björsing
paragraphs: Anton Björsing is a Swedish furniture designer based in Landskrona. He trained as a cabinet maker, studied furniture craft and design at Stenebyskolan and Malmstens, and later studied interior architecture at Chelsea College of Art and Design in London. He set up his own studio in 2013.

For Gärsnäs he designed the Vyn armchair and easy chair (2024), in solid oak with bent-wood legs and upholstered seat and back. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Gärsnäs, among them armchairs and chairs.
sources: Scandinavian Design: Vyn armchair and easy chair for Gärsnäs

designers:jean-boris-lacroix.name: Jean-Boris Lacroix
paragraphs: Jean-Boris Lacroix (1902–1984) was a French designer of lighting and furniture. Lacroix began in 1920 in the workshop of Paul Dumas and was artistic director of the Vionnet fashion house from 1924 to 1937. Lacroix combined glass and metal in his lamps, and was among the first to use brightly coloured acrylic in lighting.
Lacroix joined the Union of Modern Artists in 1945. On Formground Lacroix is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them ceiling lamps, floor lamps and wall lamps.
facts: Ceiling lamps, floor lamps, wall lamps (as shown on Formground)

designers:jerszy-seymour.name: Jerszy Seymour
paragraphs: Jerszy Seymour is a designer born in Berlin in 1968 who grew up in London. Seymour studied industrial design at the Royal College of Art, lived in Milan, and in 2004 moved to Berlin, where the Jerszy Seymour Design Workshop works on products, furniture, installations and experimental projects.

Among the projects are 'House in a Box' (2002) and the installation 'Living Systems' at the Vitra Design Museum (2007). Seymour has designed for Magis, Vitra and Alessi. On Formground Seymour is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them a ladder, mirror, stool and vase.
facts: Ladder, mirror, stool, vase (as shown on Formground)

designers:john-tree.name: John Tree
paragraphs: John Tree is a British product designer based in London. Projects listed on johntree.net include chairs and stools, lighting, a side table and electronics, made with clients such as HAY, Muuto, Allermuir, Tala and Motorola. A Sony audio-visual system was developed together with Jasper Morrison.

The Jiro chair, designed for the New Zealand brand Resident, has an oak plywood seat and a flexible T-shaped backrest on a die-cast base. On Formground John Tree is credited on {count} pieces shown through Resident, among them stools and chairs.
sources: Dezeen: Jiro Swivel Chair for Resident (partnership content)

designers:joseph-andre-motte.name: Joseph-André Motte
paragraphs: Joseph-André Motte (1925–2013) was a French furniture and interior designer. Motte trained in Paris at the École nationale supérieure des arts appliqués et des métiers d'art, graduating in 1948, and in 1954 co-founded the Atelier de Recherche Plastique with Pierre Guariche and Michel Mortier.

Motte's agency worked on interiors for Paris Métro stations and for Orly and Roissy airports, and his furniture was published by firms including Steiner and Disderot. On Formground Motte is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, all chairs.
sources: Wikipedia: Joseph-André Motte (dates, training, Atelier de Recherche Plastique)

designers:maria-bruun.name: Maria Bruun
paragraphs: Maria Bruun is a Danish furniture designer with a studio in Copenhagen. A graduate of the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts School of Design, Bruun works with sculptural furniture, interiors and exhibitions, favouring wood alongside metal and glass.

Bruun is Head of Design at Fredericia and has drawn the Pioneer Stool and the Islets series of dining, coffee and side tables for the company. On Formground Bruun is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fredericia, among them dining, coffee and side tables and a stool.
facts: Dining table, coffee table, side table, stool (as shown on Formground)

designers:matti-klenell.name: Matti Klenell
paragraphs: Matti Klenell is a Swedish designer born in 1972 and based in Stockholm. Klenell took a master's degree at Konstfack, graduating in 1999, and founded Matti Klenell Studio in 2000. The studio's work covers furniture, lighting, glassware and hand-blown glass objects, for makers such as Iittala, Marimekko, Offecct and FontanaArte.

Klenell received the Ljunggren Design Prize in 2003 and is represented in the collection of the Swedish National Museum. On Formground Klenell is credited on {count} pieces shown through Källemo and Gärsnäs, among them chairs, sofas and tables.
facts: Chairs, sofas, tables (as shown on Formground)

designers:michael-young.name: Michael Young
paragraphs: Michael Young is a British industrial designer, born in Sunderland in 1966, who studied at Kingston University and worked with Tom Dixon in London. Michael Young Studio, founded in 1993 and now based in Hong Kong and Tokyo, designs products, furniture and lighting, with clients including KEF, Steelcase and Georg Jensen.

Young's Drift Pendant was made for Resident. On Formground Michael Young is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, WonderGlass and Resident, among them a bar stool, a pendant lamp and objects.
facts: Bar stool, pendant lamp, objects (as shown on Formground)

designers:nina-jobs.name: Nina Jobs
paragraphs: Nina Jobs is a Swedish designer who began in graphic design and then studied product design at the École nationale supérieure des Arts Décoratifs in Paris. Jobs began working solo in 2000, and the portfolio covers furniture, textiles, lighting, glass and graphics for clients such as Design House Stockholm, Ikea, Svenskt Tenn and Skandiform.

The Poppy Poufs for Fogia show a typical approach: clean geometry, soft volume and colour used as the main expression. On Formground Nina Jobs is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fogia and Gärsnäs, among them ottomans and sofas.

designers:olsson-lyckefors.name: Olsson Lyckefors
paragraphs: Olsson Lyckefors is an architecture studio in Gothenburg, Sweden. It was founded in 2012 as Bornstein Lyckefors and took its present name, Olsson Lyckefors Arkitektur, in August 2022. Johan Olsson and Andreas Lyckefors, who lead the studio, met as students at Chalmers School of Architecture.
Projects range from housing and commercial buildings to interiors, public buildings and exhibition spaces, among them the Polestar headquarters from 2018. More work is shown on the studio's site.

designers:omri-revesz.name: Omri Revesz
paragraphs: Omri Revesz is a designer born in Tel Aviv in 1980 who graduated from IUAV in Venice, where Revesz runs Omri Revesz Design, a multidisciplinary studio. The studio's work ranges from industrial products and lighting to interiors, exhibitions and urban public spaces, and Revesz teaches design at IUAV.

Street Cinema, a project for the Venice Film Festival, received a Compasso d'Oro honourable mention in 2020. On Formground Omri Revesz is credited on {count} pieces shown through Mingardo, among them console tables, screens and benches.
facts: Console tables, screens, benches (as shown on Formground)

designers:tore-ahlsen.name: Tore Ahlsén
paragraphs: Tore Ahlsén (1906–1991) was a Swedish architect, born in Stockholm. Together with his brother Erik, Ahlsén worked on buildings associated with Sweden's welfare-state architecture, among them the PUB building in Stockholm and Medborgarhuset in Örebro.

Ahlsén also drew the first Pia lamps in the 1940s, a sphere of silver wire covered in removable white cotton fabric, and the Pia garden chairs. Gärsnäs took over production of the Pia lamps in the mid-1970s. On Formground Ahlsén is credited on {count} pieces shown through Gärsnäs, among them lamps and chairs.
sources: Scandinavian Design: Pia Mandarin for Gärsnäs

designers:adrien-rovero.name: Adrien Rovero
paragraphs: Adrien Rovero is a Swiss designer, born in 1981, who holds a master's degree in industrial design from ECAL in Lausanne. Rovero opened a studio in Renens in 2006 and works across furniture, lighting, objects and exhibition design, often with craftspeople and small production runs.

Early pieces include the Pimp series of anodised aluminium tables and stools for Galerie Kreo (2007) and the Pomy stool for Pfister. Rovero has also designed for Hermès and Cristallerie Saint-Louis. On Formground Adrien Rovero is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them carpets.

designers:anna-kraitz.name: Anna Kraitz
paragraphs: Anna Kraitz is a Swedish designer, born in Ängelholm, who studied at Beckmans School of Design in Stockholm in 1997–1999. Kraitz has worked with Källemo since 2000 and is represented at the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm.

Awards listed on the designer's site include the Ljunggrenska Formgivarpriset (2002) and the Bruno Mathsson Prize (2008). On Formground Anna Kraitz is credited on {count} pieces shown through Källemo, among them an armchair, a sofa and a coat stand.
facts: Armchair, sofa, coat stand (as shown on Formground)

designers:carina-seth-andersson.name: Carina Seth Andersson
paragraphs: Carina Seth Andersson is a Swedish designer, born in Stockholm in 1965, who studied at the Orrefors glass school in 1987 and took an MFA at Konstfack. Seth Andersson has worked solo since 1993 from a studio in Gustavsberg and is known mainly for glass and ceramics.

Commissions include work for Arket, Svenskt Tenn, Iittala and Marimekko, and pieces are held by the Victoria and Albert Museum and the Nationalmuseum. On Formground Carina Seth Andersson is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fogia, all vases.

designers:alessandro-stabile.name: Alessandro Stabile
paragraphs: Alessandro Stabile is an Italian designer, born in Milan in 1985, who graduated from the Faculty of Design at Politecnico di Milano in 2007. After working with Giulio Iacchetti from 2008, Stabile founded Alessandro Stabile Design Studio in Milan in 2011.

The studio's site lists work for Alessi, Magis, Moleskine and De'Longhi, among others, and Stabile has also designed for Mingardo. On Formground Alessandro Stabile is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi and Mingardo, among them lamps, thermo-insulated bottles and a table.
facts: Lamps, thermo-insulated bottles, table (as shown on Formground)
sources: Mingardo: Alessandro Stabile (birth, training, studio founding)

designers:edward-van-vliet.name: Edward van Vliet
paragraphs: Edward van Vliet is a designer working in product and interior design for private and commercial spaces. He studied architecture, interior design and industrial design at the Design Academy Eindhoven and the HKU School of the Arts in Utrecht, and founded his own studio in 1990.

He has collaborated with Moooi, &Tradition and Moroso, and designed the Develius sofa for &Tradition. The studio's site gives a Barcelona address and presents hospitality, luxury and wellness projects. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through &Tradition, among them modular sofas and coffee tables.
facts: Modular sofas, coffee tables (as shown on Formground)
sources: smow: Edward van Vliet (training, studio founded 1990, collaborations)

designers:florence-knoll.name: Florence Knoll
paragraphs: Florence Knoll (1917-2019), later Florence Knoll Bassett, was an American architect, interior designer and furniture designer, born in Saginaw, Michigan. She studied at Cranbrook, the Architectural Association in London and the Illinois Institute of Technology, where she studied under Mies van der Rohe.

In 1943 she founded the Knoll Planning Unit, the interior design service of Knoll Associates, and directed it until 1965. Her furniture for Knoll includes the Parallel Bar Lounge Chair and a coffee table. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them sofas and chairs.
sources: Knoll: Defining Modern, ten years later
Cranbrook Art Museum: Florence Knoll Bassett, Armchair
Wikipedia: Florence Knoll (dates, training, Planning Unit)

designers:gunnar-asplund.name: Gunnar Asplund
paragraphs: Gunnar Asplund (1885-1940) was a Swedish architect, born and died in Stockholm, and a key figure of Nordic Classicism in the 1920s. He became professor of architecture at the Royal Institute of Technology in 1931 and designed Stockholm Public Library, built 1924-1928, and, with Sigurd Lewerentz, the Skogskyrkogården cemetery.

His furniture and lighting include the GA-2 armchair, made for Nordiska Kompaniet in 1931 and later produced by Källemo, and the GA6 lamp for Gothenburg City Hall (1937). On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Källemo, among them chairs, armchairs and lights.
facts: Chairs, armchairs, lights (as shown on Formground)

designers:jim-hannon-tan.name: Jim Hannon-Tan
paragraphs: Jim Hannon-Tan is a product designer born in Spain and raised in Australia, who spent 15 years in Europe developing his skills in Milan, London and Amsterdam. In Amsterdam he held a senior role at Marcel Wanders Studio.

He now runs Jim Hannon-Tan Design, a studio based in Australia. His work draws on the convergence of art and technology. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them nutcrackers.

designers:jonas-wagell.name: Jonas Wagell
paragraphs: Jonas Wagell is a Swedish architect and designer who runs the Stockholm studio Jonas Wagell Design & Architecture (JWDA). He graduated from Konstfack in Stockholm in 2007 and also trained at Berghs School of Communication and Parsons School of Design in New York.

The studio works mainly on product and furniture design, especially soft seating and lighting, including the Julep sofa for Tacchini and the Panorama modular sofa for Wendelbo. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Frandsen, among them table lamps, pendants and ceiling lamps.
facts: Table lamps, pendants, ceiling lamps (as shown on Formground)

designers:jrgen-gammelgaard.name: Jørgen Gammelgaard
paragraphs: Jørgen Gammelgaard (1938-1991) was a Danish furniture designer and cabinetmaker. He studied at the Royal Academy's furniture school under Ole Wanscher and Poul Kjærholm, worked in Arne Jacobsen's studio and founded his own practice in 1973.

His designs include the Skagen chair, developed with Børge Schiang in the early 1980s, and the EJ20 sofa for Erik Jørgensen. He also consulted for UNESCO on projects in Samoa, Sri Lanka and Sudan. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fredericia, among them coffee tables, dining tables and stools.
facts: Coffee tables, dining tables, stools (as shown on Formground)

designers:keiji-takeuchi.name: Keiji Takeuchi
paragraphs: Keiji Takeuchi is a Japanese-born, Milan-based designer. He was born in Fukuoka, grew up mostly in New Zealand, and studied on a scholarship at ENSCI / Les Ateliers in Paris. After working for Naoto Fukasawa he moved to Milan in 2012 and set up his own design office in 2015.

His clients include MillerKnoll, Boffi De Padova and Karimoku, and in 2024 he curated the exhibition Walking Sticks & Canes at Triennale Milano. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fredericia and Alessi, among them coffee grinders, stools and side tables.
facts: Coffee grinders, stools, side tables (as shown on Formground)

designers:luigi-caccia-dominioni.name: Luigi Caccia Dominioni
paragraphs: Luigi Caccia Dominioni (1913-2016) was an Italian architect and designer from Milan. He graduated from the Politecnico di Milano in 1936 and opened a studio with Livio and Pier Giacomo Castiglioni.

In 1947 he co-founded the furniture company Azucena with Ignazio Gardella and Corrado Corradi dell'Acqua, for which he designed the Monachella lamp (1953) and the Catilina armchair (1958). His Caccia flatware is now reissued by Alessi. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them cutlery sets and ladles.
facts: Cutlery sets, ladles (as shown on Formground)

designers:paolo-ulian.name: Paolo Ulian
paragraphs: Paolo Ulian, born in Massa Carrara in 1961, studied painting at the Academy of Fine Arts in Carrara and graduated in industrial design from ISIA in Florence in 1990. He then worked with Enzo Mari until 1992 and returned to Tuscany to open a studio with his brother Giuseppe.

Ulian is known for objects that often reuse industrial waste. His first production projects, in 1995, were with Driade and Bieffeplast, and he has also worked with Droog Design, Fontana Arte and Danese. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them wine coolers, containers and baskets.
facts: Wine coolers, containers, baskets and bowls (as shown on Formground)

designers:sabine-marcelis.name: Sabine Marcelis
paragraphs: Sabine Marcelis is a Dutch artist and designer, born in 1985 in Alkmaar. She studied industrial design at Victoria University of Wellington and graduated from the Design Academy Eindhoven in 2011, after which she set up Studio Sabine Marcelis in Rotterdam.

Her work centres on transparency, reflection and translucency, with materials such as resin, glass and stone, and is held by MoMA, the Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam and the Vitra Design Museum, among others. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through BD Barcelona, among them chairs.

designers:stefan-borselius.name: Stefan Borselius
paragraphs: Stefan Borselius is a Swedish designer who trained in woodworking, attended Steneby School and the Carl Malmsten furniture school, and studied at Konstfack in Stockholm. He set up his studio in 2002, straight after graduating.

His work covers furniture and interior design, from chairs and lamps to room dividers, carpets and textiles. It includes the Sting aluminium chair with Fredrik Mattson for Blå Station and the Sam table for Fogia, made with Note Design Studio and Andreas Engesvik. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fogia, among them chairs and lounge chairs.
facts: Chairs, lounge chairs (as shown on Formground)

designers:studio-piet-boon.name: Studio Piet Boon
paragraphs: Studio Piet Boon is a design studio founded in 1983 by the Dutch designer Piet Boon. It works in exterior, interior and product design, with projects across private, hospitality, office and real estate development, such as Rosewood Amsterdam and Andaz Hotel Seoul Gangnam.

For Serax the studio designs Base, a tableware line of dinnerware, cutlery and glassware, as well as vases, flower pots and interior accessories. On Formground Studio Piet Boon is credited on {count} pieces shown through Serax, among them vases.

designers:taf.name: Taf
paragraphs: TAF Architects (Taf) is a Stockholm studio run by Gabriella Gustafson and Mattias Ståhlbom, who have worked together since 2002. It designs lighting, furniture and interiors in the space between architecture and design, and works from a refurbished bakery in the city centre.

Its Wood Lamp drew international attention, and with Skagerak it made the Overlap table and bench. The studio's work has been shown at MoMA and is in the collections of the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm and the Danish Design Museum. On Formground Taf is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fogia, among them lounge chairs, sofas and side tables.
facts: Lounge chairs, sofas, side tables (as shown on Formground)

designers:timo-ripatti.name: Timo Ripatti
paragraphs: Timo Ripatti is a Finnish designer and architect, educated as a furniture designer. He leads Studio Ripatti in Turku, which works with lighting and product design for clients across Europe.

His work history runs from lighting and furniture to large architectural, exhibition and interior projects, and he teaches furniture design at Aalto University in Helsinki. He designed the Huilu pendant and wall luminaire for the Swedish lighting maker Blond Belysning, and the U-Light collection for Axolight. Studio Ripatti's site presents his work and contact details.
sources: Scandinavian Design: Huilu by Timo Ripatti for Blond Belysning

designers:viggo-boesen.name: Viggo Boesen
paragraphs: Viggo Boesen was a Danish architect and furniture designer, born in Copenhagen in 1907. He studied architecture at the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts, where he met Finn Juhl, and he worked in a functionalist spirit, often in rattan.

His Fox chair won the Danish wicker-makers' guild competition in 1936, and the Little Petra armchair and sofa followed in 1938, of which only about 30 were made in his lifetime. He died in 1985. On Formground Viggo Boesen is credited on {count} pieces shown through &Tradition, among them lounge chairs and a two-seater sofa.
facts: Lounge chairs, 2-seater sofas (as shown on Formground)
sources: Vogue Scandinavia: Viggo Boesen's belated break

designers:vittorio-zecchin.name: Vittorio Zecchin
paragraphs: Vittorio Zecchin (1878-1947) was an Italian painter and glass designer, born in Murano as the son of a glassblower. He trained at the Accademia di Belle Arti in Venice.

From 1921 to 1925 he was artistic director of Vetri Soffiati Muranesi Cappellin Venini & C., where he made thin-walled blown glass in simple shapes and colours, drawing on the vessels shown in sixteenth-century Venetian paintings. In the 1930s he worked with several Murano glassworks and taught at glass schools. On Formground Vittorio Zecchin is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them vases and lighting.
sources: Wikipedia (Italian): Vittorio Zecchin (dates, training, glassworks, teaching)

designers:zaha-hadid.name: Zaha Hadid
paragraphs: Zaha Hadid (1950-2016) was an Iraqi-British architect, born in Baghdad. She studied mathematics at the American University of Beirut and then architecture at the Architectural Association in London, and opened Zaha Hadid Architects in London in 1980.

Alongside buildings, she designed objects for Alessi, including the Crevasse vase in mirror-polished steel (2005) and the Forma cheese grater, and the glassmaker WonderGlass lists her among its designers. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi and WonderGlass, among them graters, vases and lighting.
facts: Graters, vases, lighting (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Zaha Hadid (birth, studies, firm founded 1980)
WorldArchitecture: Zaha Hadid's Forma grater for Alessi

designers:adam-shirley.name: Adam Shirley
paragraphs: Adam Shirley is a designer whom Dwell credits as coming from Cranbrook. He has designed tabletop objects for the Italian maker Alessi, among them the V Tray and the Pinch vase.

The V Tray is made of stainless steel by bending a rectangular sheet five times at alternating 45-degree angles, and it is also made in a black resin-coated version. On Formground Adam Shirley is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them vases and trays.

designers:andreas-martin-lof.name: Andreas Martin-Löf
paragraphs: Andreas Martin-Löf is a Swedish architect who founded the Stockholm practice Andreas Martin-Löf Arkitekter (AML) in 2008. The practice is best known for architecture, with projects ranging from student housing to a summer house, and it also designs products.

Among them is the A.M.L. Clamp Light, a lamp from 2009 with a folded brass clamp for attaching it to shelves, made with components from Swedish suppliers. Monocle has also written about the studio's Stockholm office.
sources: Monocle: Andreas Martin-Löf on designing the perfect Stockholm office
Dezeen: A.M.L. Clamp Light by Andreas Martin-Löf

designers:bertrand-lavier.name: Bertrand Lavier
paragraphs: Bertrand Lavier is a French conceptual artist, painter and sculptor, born in 1949 in Châtillon-sur-Seine. He studied at the École Nationale Supérieure d'Horticulture in Versailles in 1968-1971 and represented France at the 1976 Venice Biennale.

His work transforms everyday objects by painting over them or by playing with their names, building on the legacy of Duchamp's readymades. Galerie Kreo lists his 1991 work Tennis Volley-Ball. On Formground Bertrand Lavier is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo.

designers:chris-kabel.name: Chris Kabel
paragraphs: Chris Kabel is a Dutch designer, born in Bloemendaal in 1975. He graduated from the Design Academy Eindhoven in 2001 and started his practice in Rotterdam in 2002, where he still lives and works.

He designs objects, furniture and architectural elements, combining an interest in materials and natural phenomena with an analytical approach. His Wood Ring, produced by Galerie Kreo, won a Dutch Design Award in 2011, and he teaches at the Hochschule für Gestaltung in Karlsruhe and at ECAL in Lausanne. On Formground Chris Kabel is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo. His site lists his products and research.

designers:cini-boeri.name: Cini Boeri
paragraphs: Cini Boeri (1924-2020) was an Italian architect and designer, born and based in Milan. She graduated in architecture from the Polytechnic University of Milan in 1951, worked with Marco Zanuso until 1963 and then opened her own studio.

She designed furniture for Arflex, among them the Strips sofa from 1972, which won the Compasso d'Oro in 1979, and also worked for Knoll, Artemide, Magis and Rosenthal. Several of her pieces are in museum collections. On Formground Cini Boeri is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo.
sources: Wikipedia: Cini Boeri (education, Zanuso, client list)

designers:daniel-rybakken.name: Daniel Rybakken
paragraphs: Daniel Rybakken is a Norwegian designer, born in 1984 and raised in Oslo. He studied design at the Oslo School of Architecture and at the School of Arts & Crafts in Gothenburg, graduated with a Master of Fine Arts in 2008 and started his own practice with bases in Gothenburg and Oslo.

He is known for lighting that studies natural daylight. His 2017 collection for Artek comprises the Kiila range of storage and seating and the 124° mirrors. On Formground Daniel Rybakken is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo and Artek, among them storage.
facts: Storage and organisation (as shown on Formground)
sources: Artek: Daniel Rybakken exhibition at the Helsinki Design Museum

designers:erik-olovsson.name: Erik Olovsson
paragraphs: Erik Olovsson is a Swedish designer and the founder of Studio EO in Stockholm, which works with furniture, product and graphic design. He studied fine art and graphic design, is a Konstfack graduate, and worked for three years as an art director at Acne.

In 2016 Studio EO presented the Indefinite Vases, seven designs that set hand-blown glass against bases of cut granite, marble and onyx. Olovsson has also designed a clothes rail with a stone base and a shelving system. On Formground Erik Olovsson is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them vases.

designers:anna-e-gian-franco-gasparini.name: Anna e Gian Franco Gasparini
paragraphs: Anna and Gian Franco Gasparini are Italian designers who work across product design and communication through their studio Architettura della Comunicazione. Gian Franco studied architecture in Florence, taught industrial design at ISIA Florence and directed the Università del Progetto in Reggio Emilia for twelve years.

For Alessi they designed the Sbriciola bread board and the K-Block knife block, and they have also made a hammer-shaped nutcracker for Coltellerie Berti. On Formground Anna e Gian Franco Gasparini are credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them chopping boards.
sources: Gessato: Anna and Gian Franco Gasparini

designers:bethan-laura-wood.name: Bethan Laura Wood
paragraphs: Bethan Laura Wood is an English multidisciplinary designer, born in 1983, working with furniture, decorative objects, lighting and installations in materials such as glass, laminated wood veneer and ceramics. She studied 3D design at Brighton University and then at the Royal College of Art, and founded her London studio in 2009.

Her studio's work is shaped by materials investigation, collaboration with artisans, and attention to colour and detail. For WonderGlass she designed the Chain fruit bowl and the Chain side table. On Formground Bethan Laura Wood is credited on {count} pieces shown through WonderGlass, among them a bowl and a side table.
facts: Bowls, side tables (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Bethan Laura Wood (training, studio founded 2009)

designers:denis-santachiara.name: Denis Santachiara
paragraphs: Denis Santachiara is an Italian designer, born in 1950 in Campagnola Emilia. He is self-taught and worked as a car stylist early in his career, before making work that sits between art and design.

In 1984 he presented the manifesto La Neomerce at the Milan Triennale, and his work has shown at the Venice Biennale (1980) and Documenta 8 in Kassel. For Baleri Italia he designed the Mama armchair and the Tato seat and footrest, both from 1995. On Formground Denis Santachiara is credited on {count} pieces shown through Baleri Italia, among them armchairs and a seat/footrest.
facts: Armchairs, seats and footrests (as shown on Formground)

designers:enzo-mari.name: Enzo Mari
paragraphs: Enzo Mari (1932-2020) was an Italian designer and artist, born in Cerano. He studied at the Brera Academy in Milan from 1952 to 1956 and took part in the Milan avant-garde of the 1950s, including the kinetic art and programmed art groups.

From 1956 he specialised in industrial design, working for Danese on pieces such as the 16 animali puzzle (1957) and the Sumatra paper tray (1976), and he taught at schools including the Politecnico di Milano. The estate manages his official site. On Formground Enzo Mari is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them trays.
sources: Enzo Mari: official site (managed by his estate)

designers:claudia-valsells.name: Clàudia Valsells
paragraphs: Clàudia Valsells (born 1969) is an artist based in Barcelona who specialises in colour. She trained as a mural painter, then spent some 20 years running her own studio, Arts&Claus, advising on colour for architecture and interiors in Spain and abroad. She also created a colour chart of more than 200 references used by architects.

Her Tones collection for nanimarquina (2022) consists of four rug models built around colour, and she designed the Edges collection of 2019 for Design Within Reach, edited by Nani Marquina. On Formground Clàudia Valsells is credited on {count} pieces shown through nanimarquina, among them indoor rugs.

designers:asca-studio.name: Asca Studio
paragraphs: Asca Studio is a design studio co-founded by Cassandra Bradfield and Sofia Olsson. It works on material-focused interiors and object design, with a stated focus on longevity and spatial sensitivity, and it has taken on hospitality, residential, retail, exhibition and product projects.

Among its projects is the interior of the Ómós restaurant and guesthouse in Abbeyleix, Ireland. The studio is among the designers represented by Resident. On Formground Asca Studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Resident, among them a chair and a stool. Its site shows projects and contact details.

designers:flemming-lassen.name: Flemming Lassen
paragraphs: Flemming Lassen (1902-1984) was a Danish architect and furniture designer born in Copenhagen. He trained as a mason, completed his education at the Technical School and worked in several architecture studios. With Arne Jacobsen he designed the House of the Future in 1929 and Søllerød Town Hall in 1942.

His furniture includes The Tired Man lounge chair, designed for the Copenhagen Cabinetmakers' Guild exhibition in the 1930s, and the Mayor sofa, made with Jacobsen. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through &Tradition, among them 3-seater and 2-seater sofas.
sources: Scandinaviandesign.com: The Tired Man, 90 Year Anniversary

designers:form-us-with-love.name: Form Us With Love
paragraphs: Form Us With Love is a design studio founded in 2005 and based in Stockholm. Its co-founders are Jonas Pettersson, who acts as design strategist, and John Löfgren, the design director. The studio designs products and also co-founded ventures: the watch company TID Watches in 2012, the building-material brand BAUX, the handwash brand FORGO and the prototyping platform Prototypa.
Its lighting work includes the modular Catena system, made with Blond and shown at Euroluce in Milan in 2025. The studio's site lists its projects, clients and team.
sources: Form Us With Love: Clients and ventures
Form Us With Love: Catena with Blond

designers:fredrik-wretman.name: Fredrik Wretman
paragraphs: Fredrik Wretman is a Swedish artist and sculptor, born in Stockholm in 1953. He studied at the Gerlesborg School, ABF's art school and the Royal Institute of Art in Stockholm, and has taught at Konstfack and the Royal Institute of Art. His site lists solo and group exhibitions from the late 1980s onwards, among them Moderna museet in Stockholm in 1991.
He began working with the Swedish furniture maker Källemo in 1992, and Källemo lists him among its designers. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Källemo, among them lights.
sources: Swedish Wikipedia: Fredrik Wretman (birth year, training)

designers:gianfranco-frattini.name: Gianfranco Frattini
paragraphs: Gianfranco Frattini (1926-2004) was an Italian architect and designer, born in Padua, who graduated in architecture from the Politecnico di Milano in 1953. After working in the office of Gio Ponti he opened his own practice in Milan. From 1954 he worked with Cassina and later with other manufacturers, and with Livio Castiglioni he designed the Boalum lamp for Artemide.

His archive, founded in 2004 by his children, maintains a website on his architecture and product design. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them coffee tables.

designers:gio-tirotto.name: Gio Tirotto
paragraphs: Gio Tirotto is an Italian designer who studied at the Politecnico di Milano and then worked with several design firms, among them that of Diego Grandi. In 2010 he founded a studio under his own name, which is based in Fiorenzuola, Italy. His work covers product design, interiors and exhibition design, and he also takes on art direction.

For Mingardo he designed the RollinGin drinks trolley, and Mingardo's designer page introduces him in his own words. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Mingardo, a trolley and a shelving piece.
sources: Salone del Mobile: Gio Tirotto, the age of timeless fine design
Mohd: RollinGin Trolley by Mingardo, designed by Gio Tirotto

designers:hideki-yoshimoto.name: Hideki Yoshimoto
paragraphs: Hideki Yoshimoto founded Tangent in 2015, a London-based design and invention brand that works at the meeting point of technology and design. In 2017 Tangent presented the installation Rise and Drift at the Maison et Objet fair in Paris with WonderGlass, a study of water bubbles and the way light passes through glass and resin.
Rise, a numbered edition, suspends hand-blown glass bubbles in a resin cube on a metal or marble plinth. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through WonderGlass, among them objects.
sources: Designboom: WonderGlass explores water bubbles at Maison et Objet

designers:holscher-design.name: Holscher Design
paragraphs: Holscher Design is a strategic product design company in Copenhagen, rooted in the Danish-Scandinavian design tradition. Its partners include Rasmus Holscher, Friederike Faller, Jette Banke, Stig Myler and Anders G. Ellegaard.

The studio's published cases cover lighting, sanitary ware, architectural hardware, furniture, mobility and electronic devices, with projects for clients such as Flos, Philips, Geberit and Vibia. On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Vibia, among them ceiling lamps and table lamps.
facts: Ceiling lamps, table lamps (as shown on Formground)

designers:india-mahdavi.name: India Mahdavi
paragraphs: India Mahdavi is an Iranian-French architect and designer, born in Tehran in 1962, who lives and works in Paris. She was artistic director for Christian Liaigre for seven years before starting on her own, and her studio was created in 2000. Its work ranges from architecture and interiors to scenography, furniture and objects.

On Rue Las Cases she has gathered a studio, a furniture showroom and a shop for small objects, Petits Objets. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through WonderGlass, among them chandeliers and objects.

designers:jens-risom.name: Jens Risom
paragraphs: Jens Risom (1916-2016) was a Danish-American furniture designer, born in Copenhagen. He studied in Copenhagen, where his teachers included Kaare Klint, and emigrated to the United States shortly before Germany invaded Denmark in 1940. In 1941 he teamed up with Hans Knoll, and in 1942 the Hans Knoll Furniture Company launched with its first 600 line, most of it designed by Risom.
The line included stools, armchairs and lounge chairs of cedar and webbing. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fredericia, among them side tables and lounge chairs.
facts: Side tables, lounge chairs (as shown on Formground)

designers:jet-dircks.name: Jet Dircks
paragraphs: Jet Dircks is the only designer who works at Pode on a permanent basis. Alongside designing, she selects the other designers who work with the furniture maker, gives them briefings, maintains contacts and gives feedback during the design process.

She designed Pode's Edit sofa, which comes in fabric or leather with distinctive piping that can be finished in a different colour or material, and the Insert modular sofa programme, which lets the buyer create the configuration an interior needs. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Pode, among them sofas and corner sofas.
facts: Sofas, corner sofas (as shown on Formground)

designers:kaare-klint.name: Kaare Klint
paragraphs: Kaare Klint (1888-1954) was a Danish architect, furniture designer and professor. Born in Frederiksberg, Copenhagen, he apprenticed as a furniture maker from 1893 and designed his first piece of furniture, the Faaborg Chair, in 1914. In 1924 he co-founded the furniture design department at the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts, where he taught precision, durability and respect for natural resources. His research into the proportions of the human body shaped his designs.
His teaching influenced Børge Mogensen and Hans J. Wegner. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fredericia, among them armchairs and dining chairs.
facts: Armchairs, dining chairs (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Kaare Klint (birth, apprenticeship, early work)

designers:la-invisible.name: La Invisible
paragraphs: La Invisible Studio was founded in 2004 by Maria Güell in Barcelona. It is a small team with a large network of collaborators, and it works on lighting as an immersive experience, balancing technical precision with a sculptural approach to illumination.

With Xavi Fernández, the studio designed the Bigger collection of pendant and ceiling lamps, its first collaboration with Vibia. The ceiling version is a surface-mounted luminaire in two sizes, with a slim or wider shade. On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Vibia, among them ceiling lamps and pendants.
facts: Ceiling lamps, pendants (as shown on Formground)

designers:leonard-kadid.name: Léonard Kadid
paragraphs: Léonard Kadid is an architect and industrial designer based in Paris. He studied at the École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne and the École d'Architecture de la Ville et des Territoires in Paris, and worked at Herzog & de Meuron in Basel. His studio spans architecture, furniture and lighting.

His solid oak chair collection Pier won the French FD100 award in 2022, and the same year his Möja lamp entered the permanent collection of the Mobilier National. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Resident, among them chairs and seating.

designers:lievore-altherr.name: Lievore Altherr
paragraphs: Lievore Altherr, earlier Lievore Altherr Molina, was a Barcelona design studio working in product design, consultancy and art direction. Jeannette Altherr was a founding partner of Lievore Altherr Molina from 1990 to 2015 and of Lievore Altherr from 2015 to 2019, and in 2019 she co-founded Altherr Désile Park.

For Vibia the studio developed many lighting collections, among them the Brisa outdoor lights, the Cosmos hanging lamps, the I.cono floor, table and wall lamps and the Skan floor and hanging lamps. On Formground it is credited on {count} pieces shown through Vibia, among them pendants and wall lamps.
facts: Pendants, wall lamps (as shown on Formground)

designers:luigi-baroli.name: Luigi Baroli
paragraphs: Luigi Baroli was born in Corbetta, in the province of Milan, and graduated in architecture from the Milan Polytechnic. He has worked in architecture, furnishings, events, communication and jewellery design, and designed furniture, handles and lamps for various companies.

He collaborated with Baleri Italia from 1988 to 2004, overseeing the artistic direction of its Milan showroom. His Cartoons screen, a free-standing screen of corrugated cardboard designed in 1992, received the Compasso d'Oro. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Baleri Italia, among them a screen and a stackable chair.
facts: Screen, stackable chair (as shown on Formground)

designers:marialaura-irvine.name: Marialaura Irvine
paragraphs: Marialaura Irvine, born in 1972, graduated in architecture in Naples, where she studied under Riccardo Dalisi, and then studied strategic design at the Politecnico di Milano. She later combined her expertise with a British design approach, working alongside her late husband James Irvine, and leads Studio Irvine, a studio in central Milan for product design, art direction and architecture.

Her clients include Arper, Muji, Thonet, Olivari and Mattiazzi, and her research is linked to mono-materiality. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Baleri Italia, among them stackable and upholstered chairs.
facts: Stackable chairs, upholstered chairs (as shown on Formground)

designers:michael-raasch.name: Michael Raasch
paragraphs: Michael Raasch is a German designer of furniture, lighting and accessories. His working philosophy, as quoted on Pode's designer page, is "the search for the 'essential'".

For the furniture maker Pode he designed the Uturn and Pom lamps. Both are available in the epoxy colours Charcoal and Biscotti, and Uturn stands 136 cm high, Pom 125 cm. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Pode, among them lighting.

designers:pier-giacomo-castiglioni.name: Pier Giacomo Castiglioni
paragraphs: Pier Giacomo Castiglioni (1913–1968) was an Italian architect and designer from Milan. He studied architecture at the Politecnico di Milano, graduating in 1937, and after the Second World War worked in a design partnership with his brother Achille.

Their work includes the Luminator and Toio lamps for Flos, radios for Brionvega and the Sella and Mezzadro stools for Zanotta. He also co-founded the Italian industrial design association ADI in 1956. On Formground Pier Giacomo Castiglioni is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them wall clocks.
sources: Wikipedia: Pier Giacomo Castiglioni (dates, training, partnership, lamps and radios)

designers:pierre-guariche.name: Pierre Guariche
paragraphs: Pierre Guariche (1926–1995) was a French designer, interior decorator and architect. He graduated from the École nationale supérieure des arts décoratifs in Paris in 1949 and worked in the studio of Marcel Gascoin. His career as a designer took off in 1950 with the publication of his first light, the Rotaflex lamp.

From 1951 he made furniture and lights for companies including Airborne and the lighting publisher Pierre Disderot, and in 1954 he co-founded the Atelier de Recherche Plastique with Michel Mortier and Joseph-André Motte. On Formground Pierre Guariche is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them wall lamps.

designers:sergio-asti.name: Sergio Asti
paragraphs: Sergio Asti (1926–2021) was an Italian architect and designer from Milan. After graduating in architecture from the Politecnico di Milano he opened his own design studio in the city and became a founder member of the Italian industrial design association ADI.

He designed the Marco glass vase for Salviati, which won a Compasso d'Oro in 1962, and worked with Brionvega, Knoll, Zanotta and others. He also designed interiors and exhibition layouts. On Formground Sergio Asti is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them sofas.
sources: Wikipedia: Sergio Asti (dates, companies, Marco vase)

designers:rodrigo-torres.name: Rodrigo Torres
paragraphs: Rodrigo Torres is a Colombian-Italian product designer based in Milan. He graduated in industrial design from Jorge Tadeo Lozano University in Bogotá in 1998 and took a master's in product design at Domus Academy in 1999.

He worked for five years in Stefano Giovannoni's studio before founding Design by Rodrigo Torres in Milan in 2004. His clients include Alessi, Poliform, Oras and Nike. On Formground Rodrigo Torres is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi.
sources: Domus Academy: Rodrigo Torres, alumni profile

designers:thomas-sandell.name: Thomas Sandell
paragraphs: Thomas Sandell is a Swedish architect and designer, born in Jakobstad, Finland, in 1959. He studied architecture at the Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm and in 1995 co-founded the Stockholm office sandellsandberg with Ulf Sandberg and Joakim Uebel, covering architecture, design and communication.

His furniture and objects have been made by manufacturers such as Artek, Svenskt Tenn, Källemo, Gärsnäs and B&B Italia, and he designed the IKEA PS collection of 1995. He also did the interiors of Moderna Museet in Stockholm. On Formground Thomas Sandell is credited on {count} pieces shown through Källemo, among them armchairs and sofas.

designers:ramon-esteve.name: Ramón Esteve
paragraphs: Ramón Esteve is a Spanish architect and designer, born in Valencia in 1964. He took his architecture degree in Madrid in 1990 and founded Ramón Esteve Estudio in Valencia the following year. He earned a doctorate at the Polytechnic University of Valencia in 1996.

The studio works across scales, from product design and furniture to houses, healthcare and cultural buildings. For Vibia he designed the Origami outdoor lights. On Formground Ramón Esteve is credited on {count} pieces shown through Vibia, among them wall lamps.

designers:teruhiro-yanagihara.name: Teruhiro Yanagihara
paragraphs: Teruhiro Yanagihara is a Japanese designer, born in Kagawa in 1976. After graduating from Osaka University of Art in 1999 he began working on his own and set up his own company in Osaka in 2002; he has been based in Kyoto since 2011.

His work spans interior and product design, art direction and branding for clients including Offecct, Pallucco and Kimura Glass, and he is creative director of Karimoku New Standard. On Formground Teruhiro Yanagihara is credited on {count} pieces shown through &Tradition, among them pendants and portable lamps.
facts: Pendants, portable lamps (as shown on Formground)

designers:poul-m-volther.name: Poul M. Volther
paragraphs: Poul M. Volther (1923–2001) was a Danish furniture designer. He trained as a cabinetmaker and studied furniture design at the Arts and Crafts School in Copenhagen, then worked from 1949 at the cooperative FDB Møbler, where he succeeded Børge Mogensen as artistic director in 1950.

He is best known for the Corona chair, which grew out of his 1953 Pyramid chair and was developed with the producer Erik Jørgensen in the early 1960s. On Formground Poul M. Volther is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fredericia, among them lounge chairs and ottomans.
facts: Lounge chairs, ottomans (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Poul Volther (training, FDB Møbler, Corona chair)

designers:victor-carrasco.name: Víctor Carrasco
paragraphs: Víctor Carrasco is a Spanish industrial designer, born in Valencia in 1974. He graduated in industrial design engineering from the Polytechnic University of Valencia in 1998 and was founder and creative and strategic director of the furniture company Viccarbe for more than nine years.

He then began developing his own projects and has designed for companies including Boffi, Glas Italia, LZF, Paola Lenti and Vibia, for which he created the Out floor lamp for indoor and outdoor use. On Formground Víctor Carrasco is credited on {count} pieces shown through Vibia, among them table lamps.

designers:thijs-smeets.name: Thijs Smeets
paragraphs: Thijs Smeets is a Dutch designer and engineer who studied industrial product design at The Hague University of Applied Sciences. He founded Studio Smeets in Amsterdam in 2007, after working at design studios in the Netherlands and New York.

His work covers furniture, consumer electronics, tableware and wellness products. He designed the Spot lounge chair series for Pode and Leolux in 2015, and his furniture collection for Gispen Today is in the collection of the Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam. On Formground Thijs Smeets is credited on {count} pieces shown through Pode, among them armchairs.

designers:studio-simple.name: Studio Simple
paragraphs: Studio Simple is a design studio and atelier run by Ann and Jeroen, who have worked together for 28 years. They make everyday objects described as functional and poetic, and have also done scenography, styling and interiors.

Their objects are mostly made of oak, combined with brass, steel, leather, glass and concrete, and have been shown at Valerie Traan Gallery and in an exhibition at Het Labo in Tokyo. For Serax they have made concrete plates, wooden plates, candleholders and lamps. On Formground Studio Simple is credited on {count} pieces shown through Serax.

designers:samuel-wilkinson.name: Samuel Wilkinson
paragraphs: Samuel Wilkinson is a London-based industrial designer who graduated in furniture and product design from Ravensbourne College of Art & Design in 2002. He worked at consultancies including Fitch, Tangerine, Conran and PearsonLloyd before starting his own studio.

His largest project is L'arbre de Flonville, a town square in Lausanne with a 16-metre metal tree and root-shaped benches, completed in 2008. He also designed the Plumen 001 light bulb, which won the Design Museum's Design of the Year in 2011. On Formground Samuel Wilkinson is credited on {count} pieces shown through &Tradition, among them pendants.

designers:wiel-arets.name: Wiel Arets
paragraphs: Wiel Arets is a Dutch architect and designer, born in Heerlen in 1955. He graduated from the Technical University of Eindhoven in 1983 and founded Wiel Arets Architects the same year, which is headquartered in Amsterdam with studios in the Netherlands, Germany and Switzerland.

He was dean of the Berlage Institute in Rotterdam from 1995 to 2002 and later led the College of Architecture at the Illinois Institute of Technology in Chicago. In 2004 he designed a coffee spoon for Alessi, one of a set by eight architects. On Formground Wiel Arets is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them electric kettles.
sources: Wikipedia: Wiel Arets (training, practice, teaching posts)
Spencer Museum of Art: coffee spoon, Alessi; Wiel Arets

designers:sakura-adachi.name: Sakura Adachi
paragraphs: Sakura Adachi is a Japanese industrial designer, born in Aichi in 1977. She took a bachelor's degree in industrial and craft design at Musashino Art University in Tokyo and a master's in industrial design at Central Saint Martins in London.

She has lived and worked in Milan since 2004 and has won awards including a Red Dot Design Award. For Alessi she designed the Food à porter lunch box and travel accessories as well as the Lovely Breeze rocking bowl. On Formground Sakura Adachi is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi.

designers:nao-iwamatsu.name: NAO IWAMATSU
paragraphs: Nao Iwamatsu is an industrial designer based in Tokyo. He was born in Nara, Japan, and holds a master's degree in industrial design from Kyoto. He works under the theme of Narrative Minimalism, giving minimal forms and clear structures a quiet, poetic presence.

After university he designed office and medical equipment for a large information-equipment maker, and he joined the design firm Takram in 2020. He designed the Light Shelf and Night Book lamps for Y.S.M, a lighting brand from Yashio, Saitama. On Formground NAO IWAMATSU is credited on {count} pieces shown through Y.S.M, among them table lamps.

designers:yonoh.name: Yonoh
paragraphs: Yonoh is a design studio in Valencia, Spain, founded by Clara del Portillo and Alex Selma, who met at a young designers' exhibition in 2004 and presented their first collection as Yonoh Studio in 2006. The studio designs furniture, lighting, cutlery, outdoor seating and shelving.

Its pieces include the Mosaico sofa for Sancal (2015), the Cabut chair for Pode (2020) and the Zeppelin cutlery for Bolia (2020). On Formground Yonoh is credited on {count} pieces shown through Pode, among them sofas and corner sofas.
facts: Sofas, corner sofas (as shown on Formground)

designers:antoni-arola-enric-rodriguez.name: Antoni Arola & Enric Rodríguez
paragraphs: Antoni Arola and Enric Rodríguez are industrial designers with a long career in lighting. Together they designed the Bamboo lamps for Vibia, an outdoor LED collection of single-stem and multiple-stem floor lamps and wall lights, conceived to extend the outdoors into interior spaces.

Arola was born in Tarragona in 1960, trained at the Eina school of design in Barcelona and founded Estudi Arola in 1994. That studio's work covers perfume bottles, lighting and large-scale interiors, and Arola received Spain's National Design Award in 2003.

designers:ben-van-berkel.name: Ben van Berkel
paragraphs: Ben van Berkel is an architect born in Utrecht, the Netherlands, in 1957. Van Berkel studied at the Rietveld Academy in Amsterdam and the Architectural Association in London, graduating in 1987. With Caroline Bos he set up Van Berkel & Bos Architectuurbureau in Amsterdam in 1988, and the practice was relaunched as UNStudio in 1998.

UNStudio's work spans architecture, urban planning, interiors and product design. Furniture credited to van Berkel includes Mychair for Walter Knoll (2008), SitTable for Prooff (2010) and the New Amsterdam Chair for Wilde + Spieth (2011).
sources: Wikipedia: Ben van Berkel (training, practice, furniture)

designers:bottcher-kayser.name: Böttcher & Kayser
paragraphs: Böttcher & Kayser is a design studio in Berlin, Germany, founded in 2007. The studio designs consumer products, furniture, lighting and interiors.

Clients include ANTA, Böwer, Johanson, Normann Copenhagen, Stelton and WON. The studio's work has received iF and Red Dot design awards and the Interior Innovation Award. Ligne Roset, one of the brands it has worked with, presents the studio on its designers page, where more of its work can be found.

designers:elisabeth-garouste-mattia-bone.name: Elisabeth Garouste & Mattia Bonetti
paragraphs: Élisabeth Garouste and Mattia Bonetti worked together on furniture design. Garouste was born in Paris in 1946, attended the Académie Charpentier and studied interior design at the École Camondo. Garouste's work includes interiors, theatre sets, furniture, glassware and wallpaper.

Bonetti was born in Lugano, Switzerland, in 1952, studied textile design there and began designing furniture in 1979. Bonetti is based in Paris. Furniture by Garouste with Bonetti has appeared in the Victoria and Albert Museum, the Centre Pompidou and the Guggenheim Museum.
sources: Wikipedia: Mattia Bonetti (birth, training, first furniture)

designers:fredrik-farg-emma-marga-blanch.name: Fredrik Färg & Emma Marga Blanche
paragraphs: Färg & Blanche is a design studio in Stockholm, Sweden, formed by the Swedish designer Fredrik Färg and Emma Marga Blanche, who was born in France. The studio produces its own collections and limited art pieces for galleries, and works with brands including BD Barcelona Design, Gärsnäs, Petite Friture and Design House Stockholm.

Its work includes the Julius armchair and sofa made by Gärsnäs, star-inlaid tables, the Heart and Knäckebröd lamps, ceramics for Petite Friture and the textile collection A Stitch in Time for Bernhardt Design. The 12-piece collection The Baker's House was shown in Stockholm in 2019.
sources: Elle Decoration UK: Färg & Blanche design duo

designers:kastholm-fabricius.name: Kastholm & Fabricius
paragraphs: Jørgen Kastholm (1931-2007) and Preben Fabricius (1931-1984) were Danish furniture designers who worked together from 1961 to 1968. Both studied interior design in Copenhagen under Finn Juhl, and in 1961 they opened a design studio in a cellar in Gentofte.

The German manufacturer Alfred Kill commissioned much of their work, and their showing at the Cologne Fair in 1966 brought their breakthrough. Their designs include the Tulip Chair, the Grasshopper Chair and the Scimitar Chair, typically in steel and leather.

designers:livio-castiglioni.name: Livio Castiglioni
paragraphs: Livio Castiglioni (1911-1979) was an Italian architect and designer, born and active in Milan. He graduated in architecture in 1936 and became best known for lighting, designing for companies including Artemide, Alessi, FontanaArte and Stilnovo.

He was the eldest of the three Castiglioni brothers and worked with Luigi Caccia Dominioni and his brothers. He was a consultant to Phonola and later to Brionvega, co-founded the Italian industrial design association ADI in 1956 and served as its president in 1959-1960. From 1972 he shared a Milan studio with his son Piero.
sources: Wikipedia: Livio Castiglioni (dates, training, ADI, clients)

designers:lodovico-meneghetti.name: Lodovico Meneghetti
paragraphs: Lodovico Meneghetti (1926-2020) was an Italian architect and urban planner, born in Novara. He graduated in architecture from the Politecnico di Milano in 1952 and worked across urban planning, architecture, furniture and design.

In 1953 he co-founded the studio Architetti Associati in Novara with Vittorio Gregotti and Giotto Stoppino; it moved to Milan in 1963 and closed in 1969. His furniture includes the Cavour armchair for the Novara firm Sim. He won the International Grand Prize at the 13th Milan Triennale for its "Free Time" introductory section, and later became a professor of urban planning at the Politecnico di Milano.
sources: Italian Wikipedia: Lodovico Meneghetti (dates, training, Architetti Associati, Cavour armchair)

designers:parisotto.name: Parisotto + Formenton
paragraphs: Parisotto + Formenton is an Italian studio founded in 1990 in Padua by Aldo Parisotto and Massimo Formenton, who met as architecture students at IUAV in Venice. A Milan office opened in 2004.

The studio works in architecture, retail and hospitality interiors, nautical interiors and product design, including projects for lighting, furniture and yacht companies. It is art director of the design brand True Design, whose collection includes the Wing kitchen. Press profiles list its projects and collaborations.
sources: Salone del Mobile: Focus on Parisotto+Formenton

designers:ramos-bassols.name: Ramos & Bassols
paragraphs: Ramos & Bassols is a product design studio founded in Barcelona in 2004 by industrial designers David Ramos and Jordi Bassols. Both studied at the Escola Superior de Disseny (ESDi) and met while working at G Bernal & Associats.

The studio designs lighting and furniture for domestic, urban and contract use, and has also worked on tableware. Clients include Vibia, Actiu, Escofet, Paola Lenti, Kristalia and Prostoria, for which it designed the Aire modular sofa. A Gold NeoCon award in 2016 went to its Longo collection for Actiu.
sources: Interiors from Spain: Ramos y Bassols

designers:sam-hecht-and-kim-colin.name: Sam Hecht and Kim Colin
paragraphs: Sam Hecht and Kim Colin are the designers behind Industrial Facility, a design studio in Clerkenwell, London, which they founded in 2002. Hecht trained as an industrial designer in London, Colin as an architect in California.

The studio designs furniture, lighting, tech accessories and everyday objects, with clients including Muji, Mattiazzi, &Tradition, Wästberg, Herman Miller and Yamaha. Hecht and Colin have been creative advisors to Herman Miller since 2008, and their work is held in collections such as MoMA, the Centre Pompidou and the V&A. The studio's site lists its works from 2002 onward.
sources: Nedgis: Industrial Facility (founding, backgrounds, Herman Miller, museums)

designers:thau-kallio.name: Thau & Kallio
paragraphs: Thau & Kallio is a design duo formed by Jakob Thau and Sami Kallio, with a studio in Copenhagen and Gothenburg. Thau graduated from the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts School of Design, and Kallio from HDK, the Gothenburg School of Design and Crafts; both are trained cabinetmakers.

Their work combines craft with industrial production and explores new materials. They have worked with &Tradition, where their best-known collection is Betty, a family of chairs, counter chairs, stools and benches, and with Fredericia, which makes their Yksi chair.
facts: Denmark and Sweden (Danish and Finnish designers)

designers:unstudio.name: UNStudio
paragraphs: UNStudio is an Amsterdam-based architecture and design practice, founded in 1988 by Ben van Berkel and Caroline Bos under the name Van Berkel en Bos Architectenbureau. It works across architecture, urban planning, interior design, and product and experience design.

Its projects include the Erasmus Bridge in Rotterdam, the Mercedes-Benz Museum in Stuttgart and Arnhem Centraal station. In furniture it designed the MYchair for Walter Knoll. The practice has offices in Amsterdam, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Frankfurt, Dubai, Melbourne and Austin, and its site presents the work.

designers:vittorio-gregotti.name: Vittorio Gregotti
paragraphs: Vittorio Gregotti (1927-2020) was an Italian architect, born in Novara and trained at the Politecnico di Milano. He edited the architecture magazine Casabella from 1955 to 1963 and founded Gregotti Associati International in 1974.

From 1953 he worked with Lodovico Meneghetti and Giotto Stoppino as Architetti Associati, a studio that also produced furniture. His buildings include the Barcelona Olympic Stadium and the Belem Cultural Centre in Lisbon. He also wrote on design, among other books Il disegno del prodotto industriale, on Italian industrial design from 1860 to 1980, published in 1986.
sources: Wikipedia: Vittorio Gregotti (dates, training, Casabella, buildings)
Italian Wikipedia: Vittorio Gregotti (Architetti Associati, 1986 book)

designers:formenton.name: Formenton
paragraphs: Parisotto + Formenton is an Italian studio founded in 1990 in Padua by Aldo Parisotto and Massimo Formenton, who met as architecture students at IUAV in Venice. A Milan office opened in 2004.

The studio works in architecture, retail and hospitality interiors, nautical interiors and product design, including projects for lighting, furniture and yacht companies. It is art director of the design brand True Design, whose collection includes the Wing kitchen. Press profiles list its projects and collaborations.
sources: Salone del Mobile: Focus on Parisotto+Formenton

designers:acconci.name: Acconci
