paragraphs: Vito Acconci (1940-2017) was an artist and designer, born in the Bronx, New York. He studied literature at the College of the Holy Cross and the University of Iowa, and became known for performance works such as Following Piece (1969).

In 1988 he founded Acconci Studio in Brooklyn, which worked on theoretical design and building. From the late 1980s he also made furniture and prototypes of houses and gardens. Later studio projects include the United Bamboo store in Tokyo (2003) and the Murinsel in Graz, Austria (2003).
sources: Wikipedia: Vito Acconci (training, Acconci Studio, furniture, projects)

designers:ake-axelsson.name: Åke Axelsson
paragraphs: Åke Axelsson (1932-2026) was a Swedish furniture and interior designer, born in Småland in southern Sweden. He trained in woodworking at Visby School of Woodwork, worked as a journeyman in Munich and then studied furniture and interior design in Stockholm from 1952 to 1957.

He ran his own workshop from 1961 and worked with the furniture maker Gärsnäs from 1963. His chairs include the Anselm chair, the Akustik chair, the Sonat armchair and the Ferdinand armchair, and he was also an owner of Gärsnäs.
On Formground Åke Axelsson is credited on {count} pieces shown through Gärsnäs, among them chairs, tables, armchairs, sofas and bar stools.
facts: Chairs, tables, armchairs, sofas, bar stools (as shown on Formground)

designers:alain-richard.name: Alain Richard
paragraphs: Alain Richard (1926-2017) was a French designer. He graduated in 1949 from the École Nationale Supérieure des Arts Décoratifs, lived in the Netherlands in the 1950s, and in 1952 founded his own agency with his wife, Jacqueline Iribe.

His projects included work for Orly airport, Crédit Agricole and Banque de France, and he designed furniture in the 1950s published by Vecchione, as well as TV stands. He worked with André Monpoix. On Formground Alain Richard is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them a bench.

designers:aldo-rossi.name: Aldo Rossi
paragraphs: Aldo Rossi (1931–1997) was an Italian architect and designer, born in Milan. He graduated from the Polytechnic University of Milan and was an editor of the architectural magazine Casabella-Continuità. In 1990 he received the Pritzker Prize for architecture.

Alongside buildings and theoretical work, Rossi designed furniture and products. In the 1980s he designed stainless steel cafetières for Alessi, among them the La Cupola espresso maker of 1988. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them espresso coffee makers.
facts: Espresso coffee makers (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Aldo Rossi (training, Pritzker Prize, Alessi products)
The Pritzker Architecture Prize: Aldo Rossi (1990 laureate)

designers:andrea-branzi.name: Andrea Branzi
paragraphs: Andrea Branzi (1938–2023) was an Italian architect and designer, born in Florence, who lived and worked in Milan for much of his career. He graduated in architecture in 1966, was a member of the avant-garde group Archizoom Associati, set up Studio Alchimia in 1976 and co-founded the Domus Academy in Milan.

He received the Compasso d'Oro for his career in 1987 and worked across industrial and experimental design, architecture and teaching. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, Ghidini 1961 and Galerie Kreo, among them sculptures, stools, vases and nutcrackers.
facts: Sculptures, stools, vases, nutcrackers (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Andrea Branzi (life, Archizoom, Studio Alchimia)

designers:andreas-sture.name: Andreas Sture
paragraphs: Andreas Sture is an industrial designer born in 1976. Sture studied at HDK in Gothenburg and holds a BFA in industrial design and an MFA in design. Sture works as a designer at White Arkitekter, the same firm as the designer Kristofer Jonsson.

With Jonsson, Sture designed the Tailor table for Karl Andersson & Söner, a flexible table in standard sizes whose leg is cast in recycled aluminium, drawing on the tradition of the old Husqvarna foundry. With Fanny Jiseborn, Sture designed the 1KM Display shelf, presented in 2016 for the same brand.
sources: Scandinavian Design: Tailor by Kristofer Jonsson and Andreas Sture

designers:anita-le-grelle.name: Anita Le Grelle
paragraphs: Anita Le Grelle was born and raised in Antwerp, where she gained her degree in graphic design. After working in advertising for a while she moved to London with her family, where she attended sculpture classes at the Royal College of Art and received a diploma in 2000.

She came to pottery in 2013, and demand for her work grew quickly enough that she continued professionally. Terres de Rêves is both the name of her company and of her collection, which includes tableware, lighting and interior accessories; her collaboration with Serax also includes scented candles. On Formground Anita Le Grelle is credited on {count} pieces shown through Serax, among them wall lamps.

designers:anna-von-schewen.name: Anna von Schewen
paragraphs: Anna von Schewen runs a design practice in Stockholm, founded in 1997. She trained at Konstfack in Stockholm, continued her studies in Helsinki and gained early professional experience in Copenhagen.

Her work spans furniture, exhibition design, interiors and architecture. For Fogia she has designed the Boxlike sofas in two and three-seater versions and the Social Club lounge chairs in a low and a high model. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fogia, among them sofas and lounge chairs.
facts: Sofas, lounge chairs (as shown on Formground)

designers:antoine-vandewoude.name: Antoine Vandewoude
paragraphs: Antoine Vandewoude is a self-taught designer who worked as a theatre technician for the Flanders Opera before setting up his own workshop in 1993. There he made bespoke furniture and restored old pieces, with fashion designer Dries Van Noten among his clients.

In 2014 Vandewoude began working in ceramics. His Pique-Fleurs collection for Serax, which includes vases and a candlestick, has a deep red glaze known as sang de boeuf. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Serax, among them vases.

designers:antonino-sciortino.name: Antonino Sciortino
paragraphs: Antonino Sciortino was born in Palermo and began forging iron at the age of eight in his father's studio. He worked mainly with soft iron, and is a former dancer and choreographer.

For Serax he designed the Metal Sculptures collections, among them side tables and iron bowls, finished by brush painting and polishing. For Lacividina he designed the tables of the Accursio collection. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Serax, among them baskets.

designers:arik-levy.name: Arik Levy
paragraphs: Arik Levy is an Israeli artist and industrial designer, born in Tel Aviv in 1963. He graduated with distinction from Art Center Europe in Switzerland in 1991 and lives and works in Paris. His work includes sculpture, installation and product design, and he has created set designs for contemporary dance and opera.

He is known for his sculptures and the Rock series; RockGrowth 808 was acquired by the Atomium in Brussels. For Vibia he designed the Wireflow pendants and the Fold lighting collection. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Vibia and Baleri Italia, among them pendants, table lamps, ceiling lamps, wall lamps and tables.
facts: Pendants, table lamps, ceiling lamps, wall lamps, tables (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Arik Levy (birth, training, Paris, Rock series, Vibia)

designers:arne-jacobsen.name: Arne Jacobsen
paragraphs: Arne Jacobsen (1902–1971) was a Danish architect and furniture designer, born and based in Copenhagen. He studied at the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts from 1924 to 1927 and set up his own office in 1930. His buildings include the Bellevue Sea Bath, Aarhus City Hall (with Erik Møller) and St Catherine's College in Oxford.

His furniture, among it the Ant chair from 1951 and the Seven Series from 1955, was made mostly in cooperation with Fritz Hansen, while his lamps were developed with Louis Poulsen. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through &Tradition, among them two- and three-seater sofas and wall, desk and floor lamps.
facts: Sofas, wall lamps, desk lamps, floor lamps (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Arne Jacobsen (training, buildings, furniture and lamp collaborations)

designers:bjorn-dahlstrom.name: Björn Dahlström
paragraphs: Björn Dahlström is a designer who founded his own design studio in 1982. He began in graphic design and soon moved to physical objects, often with a distinctly graphic expression, and has designed furniture, bicycles, toys, rugs, drinking glasses and carafes.

His BD1 armchair, which resembles a comma, was launched in Milan in 1994. His work is held in museums including the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm and the Victoria and Albert Museum in London. On Formground Björn Dahlström is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fogia, among them coffee tables and lounge chairs.
facts: Coffee tables, lounge chairs (as shown on Formground)

designers:bo-westerdahl.name: Bo Westerdahl
paragraphs: Bo Westerdahl is a Swedish-born furniture designer who studied furniture design and cabinetmaking at Carl Malmsten's school in Stockholm and continued his studies in Prague. He set up his own design practice in 1975.
For Fogia he designed the Boss series, a family of cabinets and sideboards. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fogia, among them sideboards and cabinets.

designers:bob-verhelst.name: Bob Verhelst
paragraphs: Bob Verhelst is a Belgian designer and set designer who studied interior architecture and scenography. He has collaborated with Dior, Chanel and Hermès on window displays, exhibitions and art installations, and has created sets for theatre productions.
For the Belgian company Serax he is developing the Yucca lighting collection. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Serax, among them table lamps.

designers:boucquillon-maaoui.name: Boucquillon & Maaoui
paragraphs: Michel Boucquillon and Donia Maaoui are Belgian designers and architects. Boucquillon specialises in industrial design and experimental architecture, while Maaoui has devoted herself in particular to sculpture and painting.

Together they created the Bark centrepiece for Alessi and the Cellule wall lamp for Martinelli Luce. Mohd's shop lists two further Alessi products under their name, the Barkroll kitchen roll holder and the Barkplace tree placeholders.

designers:branch-creative.name: Branch Creative
paragraphs: Branch Creative is an industrial design and brand consultancy based in San Francisco. Founded by Josh Morenstein, the studio works hands-on with sketches, models and prototypes, and its projects range from furniture to electronics, including razors, espresso equipment, fans and air purifiers.

Clients named on the studio's site include Fellow, Atlas, Windmill and Ghidini 1961, for which it designed Dusk Dawn. More projects are shown on the studio's site. On Formground Branch Creative is credited on {count} pieces shown through Ghidini 1961, among them chairs and tables.

designers:brge-mogensen.name: Børge Mogensen
paragraphs: Børge Mogensen (1914-1972) was a Danish furniture designer, born in Aarhus. He started as a cabinetmaker in 1934 and studied at the Danish School of Arts and Crafts and the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts.

From 1942 to 1950 he managed FDB's furniture design studio in Copenhagen, then left to found his own studio. Fredericia calls him its founding designer from 1955. His designs include a redesigned Spanish chair in 1959 and the Øresund shelving series. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fredericia, among them sofas, lounge chairs, dining chairs, dining tables and armchairs.
facts: Sofas, lounge chairs, dining chairs, dining tables, armchairs (as shown on Formground)

designers:brynjar-sigurarson.name: Brynjar Sigurðarson
paragraphs: Brynjar Sigurðarson is a designer from Iceland, born in 1986. He received a master's degree in product design from ECAL in Lausanne in 2011 and a bachelor's degree from the Iceland Academy of the Arts in Reykjavík, and has taught at ECAL's master's department. He founded Studio Brynjar & Veronika in 2014.

His work is tied to storytelling and Icelandic culture, in particular the fishing harbour environment, and ranges from drawings, photography and video to furniture such as The Silent Village tables. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them vases and coffee, side and dining tables.
facts: Vases, side tables, coffee tables, dining tables (as shown on Formground)

designers:catherine-martin.name: Catherine Martin
paragraphs: Catherine Martin is an Australian costume designer, production designer, set designer and film producer, born in 1965 and best known for her frequent collaborations with the director Baz Luhrmann. She provided both the costumes and the production design on Strictly Ballroom (1992).
She has won four Academy Awards, two for Moulin Rouge! (2001) and two for The Great Gatsby (2013). On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Serax, among them vases and bowls.

designers:cheshire-architects.name: Cheshire Architects
paragraphs: Cheshire Architects is a design studio founded in 2004 by Pip and Nat Cheshire. It has offices in Auckland, Wellington and Mount Maunganui and works internationally from New Zealand.

The studio covers masterplanning, urban design, architecture, interior, furniture, graphic and packaging design, and project management. Its projects include the Britomart district and the Hotel Britomart in Auckland. On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Resident, among them table lamps, pendant lamps and floor lamps.
facts: Table lamps, pendant lamps, floor lamps (as shown on Formground)

designers:clare-brass.name: Clare Brass
paragraphs: Clare Brass is a designer born in London in 1962 who studied at Middlesex Polytechnic. She lives and works in Milan. She collaborated with Andrea Branzi before setting up her own studio, Zoo design, and is one of the founders of the Doc group.
For Alessi, Brass designed the Kalistò kitchen boxes. On Formground Clare Brass is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, all jars.

designers:damian-williamson.name: Damian Williamson
paragraphs: Damian Williamson (1974-2024) was a furniture and product designer. He studied product design at Kingston University in London and in 2004 founded his design firm, Damian Williamson Office For Design, in Stockholm.

His work stood between British and Swedish aesthetics, with sleek and sculptural designs rooted in functionality and materials, and he was a guest lecturer at LTH University in Sweden. Wallpaper* put him on its Hot 100 list in 2007. For Fredericia he designed sofas, among them the Konami sofa. On Formground Damian Williamson is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fredericia, among them sofas.

designers:dan-yeffet.name: Dan Yeffet
paragraphs: Dan Yeffet is an Israeli-born, Paris-based designer. He studied at the Bezalel Academy in Jerusalem and graduated in product design from the Gerrit Rietveld Academie in Amsterdam in 2002. After graduating he formed his studio in Amsterdam, and in 2005 the studio moved to Paris.

His work includes furniture, glass sculptures, lights, objects, conceptual and urban spaces, gallery objects and limited series. Pieces for WonderGlass include Bouchon and Prism. On Formground Yeffet is credited on {count} pieces shown through WonderGlass, among them objects and lighting.

designers:david-dubois.name: David Dubois
paragraphs: David Dubois is a designer and scenographer from France, born in 1971. He graduated from the École Nationale Supérieure de Création Industrielle in Paris in 2003 and founded his studio, duboisproduct, in 2005. He lives and works in Paris.

His work combines, recycles and adapts everyday objects, with a particular interest in textiles and flexible materials. He has collaborated with Bless, Issey Miyake, Lalique and Christian Lacroix. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them coffee tables, wall lamps, mirrors and desks.
facts: Coffee tables, wall lamps, mirrors, desks (as shown on Formground)

designers:david-ericsson.name: David Ericsson
paragraphs: David Ericsson is a furniture designer who runs David Ericsson Design Studio. In an interview published by Gärsnäs, Ericsson names beech as a favourite material, usually starts with wood and pairs it with other materials, and seeks inspiration in Swedish, European and ancient furniture history.

The Madonna chair is a lightweight beech chair that draws on the Italian Chiavari chair and the Swedish step stool. It was designed as a new official chair for Danish state banquets for the Hans J. Wegner centenary exhibition at the Art Museum of South Jutland, where Ericsson represented Sweden. On Formground Ericsson is credited on {count} pieces shown through Gärsnäs and Källemo, among them chairs, cabinets and armchairs.
facts: Chairs, cabinets, armchairs (as shown on Formground)

designers:diego-fortunato.name: Diego Fortunato
paragraphs: Diego Fortunato is a self-taught artist and designer who started a product design career in 1995, when a manufacturer asked for a chair design. Besides product design, the work has included sculptures, art installations, graphic design and branding.

Projects include the Stone-Wool rugs collection for Nani Marquina, the Jazz lamp for Vibia and the Sit Street Furniture collection for Escofet. From 2012 to 2019 Fortunato was creative director at the Coll & Cortés Gallery, and from 2015 at Colnaghi, whose gallery on Bury Street in London was designed in 2016.
On Formground Diego Fortunato is credited on {count} pieces shown through nanimarquina and Vibia, among them indoor rugs, table lamps and pendants.
facts: Indoor rugs, table lamps, pendants (as shown on Formground)

designers:diez-office.name: Diez Office
paragraphs: Diez Office is the design practice of industrial designer Stefan Diez, who founded his studio in 2002. The practice is structured across Diez Office in Bassano del Grappa, Italy, and a studio in Munich, and designs furniture, lighting, architectural elements and accessories with a focus on the circular economy.

Its approach is framed by Stefan Diez's 10 Circular Design Guidelines, a set of principles for more responsible industrial production. On Formground Diez Office is credited on {count} pieces shown through Vibia, among them ceiling lamps, wall lamps, table lamps and pendants.
facts: Ceiling lamps, wall lamps, table lamps, pendants (as shown on Formground)

designers:dirk-winkel.name: Dirk Winkel
paragraphs: Dirk Winkel is a product designer based in Berlin who specialises in lighting and furniture. He graduated from the University of Arts (UdK) Berlin and completed an MA in Design Products at the Royal College of Art in London in 2010.
Dirk Winkel Design Office was set up in Berlin in summer 2011. He has taught Design Construction at UdK since 2012 and was appointed guest professor for product design at HBKsaar in 2022.
On Formground Dirk Winkel is credited on {count} pieces shown through Wästberg, among them suspension lamps, base lamps, wall lamps and floor lamps.
facts: Suspension lamps, base lamps, wall lamps, floor lamps, pin lamps (as shown on Formground)

designers:eduardo-chillida.name: Eduardo Chillida
paragraphs: Eduardo Chillida (1924–2002) was a Spanish Basque sculptor, born in San Sebastián. He studied architecture at the University of Madrid from 1943 to 1946, left it for art in 1947 and moved to Paris the following year, where he set up his first studio.

He worked in forged iron, steel and alabaster, often on a monumental scale, and many of his sculpture titles are in Basque; by the early 1970s his steel works stood outside the UNESCO headquarters in Paris. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through nanimarquina, among them indoor rugs and tapestries.
facts: Indoor rugs, tapestries (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Eduardo Chillida (life, training, materials, public works)
Eduardo Chillida (official site of the Foundation)

designers:edward-barber-jay-osgerby.name: Edward Barber & Jay Osgerby
paragraphs: Barber Osgerby is a design studio in East London, founded in 1996 by Edward Barber and Jay Osgerby, who studied architecture at the Royal College of Art. The studio works across architecture, interiors, sculpture, product design and exhibition design, often drawing on industrial processes and new technologies.

Its work includes the Loop Table for Isokon (1996), the 2012 Olympic torch and Soft Work for Vitra (2018). The partners also set up Universal Design Studio in 2001. The studio's site presents its projects.

designers:eero-aarnio.name: Eero Aarnio
paragraphs: Eero Aarnio is a Finnish designer, born in Helsinki in 1932. He studied at the Institute of Industrial Arts in Helsinki, graduated in 1960 and started his own office in 1962.

He is known for 1960s furniture in plastic and fibreglass, among them the Ball Chair from 1963, the Bubble Chair and the Pastil Chair. His household objects include the Citrus squeezer for Alessi. His site presents his work. On Formground Eero Aarnio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them citrus squeezers.
sources: Wikipedia: Eero Aarnio (birth, training, office, chairs)

designers:elena-salmistraro.name: Elena Salmistraro
paragraphs: Elena Salmistraro is an Italian designer and artist based in Milan. She studied at the Brera School of Art and holds degrees in fashion design (2003) and industrial design (2008) from the Polytechnic University of Milan. In 2009 she co-founded a design studio with the architect Angelo Stoli. Her work spans product design, textiles, interior installations and visual art, with vivid colours and three-dimensional textures, and she teaches at Istituto Marangoni and the Milan Polytechnic. Her own site presents design, interior and installation work, art and press.
On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi and WonderGlass, among them Christmas tree ornaments and objects.
facts: Christmas tree ornaments, objects (as shown on Formground)
sources: Living Edge: Elena Salmistraro (training, studio, teaching)

designers:elisa-giovannoni.name: Elisa Giovannoni
paragraphs: Elisa Giovannoni, also listed as Elisa Gargan, is an industrial and interior designer born in Pordenone in 1960 and listed in Milan, Italy. She specialised in industrial design at the Scuola Politecnica di Design and worked with Michele De Lucchi from 1986 to 1991. She is a founding member of Giovannoni Design with her partner Stefano, and designs for brands including Alessi, Magis, Slamp and Bisazza. She teaches at the Domus Academy and the Polytechnic School of Design.
On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Ghidini 1961 and Alessi, among them lounge chairs, armchairs, ottomans, cabinets and dining tables.
facts: Lounge chairs, armchairs, ottomans, cabinets, dining tables (as shown on Formground)
sources: Stylepark: Elisa Gargan (birth, training, studio, address)

designers:emilie-cathelineau.name: Émilie Cathelineau
paragraphs: Émilie Cathelineau is a French designer known especially for lighting. She has worked with CVL Luminaires since 2003 and has created more than ten lines for the brand.

Her lamps mix Art Deco ideas with contemporary trends, and her ranges for CVL include Paradoxe, Airy, Strate, Storm, Ruban, Compass, Pirouette, Earth and Naboo, as suspension, ceiling, wall, table and floor lamps. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through CVL, among them wall lamps, pendants, floor lamps, table lamps and ceiling lamps.
facts: Wall lamps, pendants, floor lamps, table lamps, ceiling lamps (as shown on Formground)

designers:emma-silvestris.name: Emma Silvestris
paragraphs: Emma Silvestris is a designer born in Salerno in 1962 who lives and works in Bari. She holds a degree in foreign literature and art history and worked as a teacher and researcher before moving into design. Since 1990 she has worked in design and taken part in the activities of Special Studio in Bari.

For Alessi she designed the Mediterraneo family, which includes a fruit holder, salad set, tealight holder and bowl, and the Nunziatella mozzarella set and slotted spoon. On Formground Emma Silvestris is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them serving plates, serving cutlery and baskets.
facts: Serving plates, serving cutlery, baskets, centre-pieces, fruit holders, stands, bowls (as shown on Formground)

designers:erik-jrgensen-studio.name: Erik Jørgensen Studio
paragraphs: Erik Jørgensen founded his furniture business in 1954 and became known for his upholstery skills. The company has combined craftsmanship with comfort, with a Scandinavian aesthetic, and its sofa collection grew out of the first sofa.

The collection is built around simple, classic sofas, among them the EJ220 sofa, which comes as two- and three-seaters. Fredericia lists Erik Jørgensen among its designers. On Formground Erik Jørgensen Studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fredericia, among them sofas.

designers:ernst-jensen.name: Ernst & Jensen
paragraphs: Ernst & Jensen is a design duo of Morten Ernst and Anne-Mette Jensen, described by Fredericia as furniture architects. Their collaboration goes back to the School of Architecture, where as students they won Erik Jørgensen's talent competition with the Waves lounge furniture.
Their approach combines symmetrical forms with organic, graphic shapes and unconventional concepts. Fredericia lists the Insula coffee tables, in several models, among their designs.

designers:estudio-persona.name: Estudio Persona
paragraphs: Estudio Persona is a design studio in Los Angeles run by the Uruguayan designers Emiliana Gonzalez and Jessie Young, who have worked together in the city since 2015.

The studio designs furniture and lighting, often with bold silhouettes, neutral tones and raw materials left without decoration, and works with local manufacturers. Its lighting includes the Phase and Bow series. On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Resident, among them pendant lamps, wall lamps and table lamps.
facts: Pendant lamps, wall lamps, table lamps (as shown on Formground)

designers:ettore-sottsass.name: Ettore Sottsass
paragraphs: Ettore Sottsass (1917-2007) was an Italian architect and designer, born in Innsbruck and raised in Turin. He graduated in architecture from the Politecnico di Torino in 1939 and became a design consultant to Olivetti in 1956.

He founded the Memphis group in Milan in 1980, and his Nuovo Milano cutlery for Alessi won the Compasso d'Oro in 1991. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, BD Barcelona and Galerie Kreo, among them cocktail shakers, saucers, serving plates and soup bowls.
facts: Cocktail shakers, saucers, serving plates, soup bowls (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Ettore Sottsass (years, training, Olivetti, Memphis, Alessi)

designers:federica-biasi.name: Federica Biasi
paragraphs: Federica Biasi is a designer who began her career in Italy, spent two years in Amsterdam, and in 2015 returned to Milan to set up Federica Biasi Studio. Her style is a formal but detailed simplicity, and she combines manual work with tradition.

Clients listed on her site include Gervasoni, Lema, Mingardo and Nason Moretti, and in 2020 she presented the Lume collection for Nespresso. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Mingardo, among them mirrors, shelving and vases.
facts: Mirrors, shelving, vases (as shown on Formground)

designers:foersom-hiort-lorenzen.name: Foersom & Hiort-Lorenzen
paragraphs: Foersom & Hiort-Lorenzen is a Danish design duo of Johannes Foersom (born 1947) and Peter Hiort-Lorenzen (born 1943), who have worked together since 1977. Foersom completed a cabinetmaker apprenticeship in Copenhagen in 1969 and graduated from the Arts and Crafts School in 1972.

Hiort-Lorenzen worked as a ship carpenter at Helsingør Shipyard from 1962 and graduated from the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts in 1968. Their designs include the Apollo chair, the Trinity chair and the Savannah lounge group.

designers:franca-helg.name: Franca Helg
paragraphs: Franca Helg (1920-1989) was an Italian architect and designer, born and died in Milan. She graduated from the Politecnico di Milano in 1945 and taught at the Istituto Universitario di Architettura di Venezia and at the Politecnico.

Helg worked with Franco Albini until his death in 1977. With Albini and Bob Noorda she won the Compasso d'Oro in 1964 for the signage, graphic design and interior design of the Milan underground. Other works include the La Rinascente store in Rome and the Museo degli Eremitani in Padua.
sources: Wikipedia: Franca Helg (dates, training, Albini, works)

designers:franco-albini.name: Franco Albini
paragraphs: Franco Albini (1905-1977) was an Italian architect and designer, born near Milan and trained at the Politecnico di Milano, where he graduated in architecture in 1929. After working for Gio Ponti he opened his own practice in 1930, and he taught at the Politecnico from 1963 until 1977.

He designed buildings, the Milan metro stations with Franca Helg and Bob Noorda, and furniture such as the Margherita cane chair of 1950 and the Luisa chair of 1955, which won a Compasso d'Oro. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, a sofa and an armchair.

designers:francois-azambourg.name: François Azambourg
paragraphs: François Azambourg is a French designer, born in 1963, who graduated from ENSAAMA in Paris and teaches at ENSCI-Les Ateliers. His work focuses on lightness and an economy of materials and processes, and he has collaborated with Cappellini, Hermès and Ligne Roset.

Galerie kreo lists him for several lamps that work without a lampshade, including the Arc lamps, and for the Estampé mirror. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them lamps and mirrors.

designers:fratelli-campana.name: Fratelli Campana
paragraphs: Humberto Campana and Fernando Campana worked together as the Campana brothers from a studio in São Paulo, Brazil. Their work turns everyday materials into furniture and objects, combining craftsmanship, sustainable production practices and advanced technologies. Since 2002 they have also made limited editions and unique pieces by hand in the studio.

Their work is held by the Centre Pompidou, MoMA in New York and the Vitra Design Museum, among others. They founded Instituto Campana in 2009, and Fernando died in 2022. On Formground the Campana brothers are credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them fruit bowls and baskets.
facts: Fruit bowls, baskets (as shown on Formground)

designers:georges-frydman.name: Georges Frydman
paragraphs: Georges Frydman, born in 1924, is a French designer influenced by modernism, functionalism and the Bauhaus. He studied at the Arts et Métiers, focusing on aeronautical model-making, and attended architecture courses at the Beaux-Arts before the war interrupted his studies. After qualifying as an architect he built his own house and designed its furniture.

In 1954 he founded Équipement Fonctionnel de l'Habitation, a company for modern furniture, and between the 1950s and 1970s he designed desks, seating, lighting, tables and storage. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them lamps.

designers:gerard-guermonprez.name: Gérard Guermonprez
paragraphs: Gérard Guermonprez (1917-2007) was a French furniture designer who trained at the Boulle School in Paris. He is known for simple, functional wooden furniture, and his 1955 series of light oak pieces with black lacquered metal legs drew attention. From 1957 he designed sideboards, tables, chairs and multifunctional storage units with the Magnani cabinetmaking workshop.
He showed at the Salon des arts ménagers for more than twenty years from 1954. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them chairs.

designers:giotto-stoppino.name: Giotto Stoppino
paragraphs: Giotto Stoppino (1926-2011) was an Italian architect and designer, born in Vigevano and died in Milan. He was a pupil of the architect Ernesto Nathan Rogers and worked with Vittorio Gregotti and Lodovico Meneghetti at Architetti Associati from 1953 to 1968, then ran a studio in architecture, urban planning and design.

His Arteluce lamp 537 has been in the permanent collection of the Museum of Modern Art in New York since 1970, and the Centre Pompidou holds his Tic-tac lamp (1970). He was president of the Association for Industrial Design (ADI) in 1982-84 and received the Compasso d'Oro, including its career award in 2011.

designers:grung-engesvik.name: Grung Engesvik
paragraphs: Grung Engesvik is a design studio in Oslo run by Andreas Engesvik and Jannicke Grung. The two have collaborated for many years, and the studio name became visible in 2026 when Jannicke Grung formally became a partner.

Andreas Engesvik co-founded the Norwegian design collective Norway Says, and his work for Fogia began in 2013 with the Tiki sofa. It has since included Bollo, Barba, Lyra and Supper, and the studio's Flora armchair is listed among Fogia's 2026 products. On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fogia, among them lounge chairs, sofas, dining tables, ottomans and stools.
facts: Lounge chairs, sofas, dining tables, ottomans, stools (as shown on Formground)

designers:guillaume-bardet.name: Guillaume Bardet
paragraphs: Guillaume Bardet is a designer, born in 1971, who graduated from the École Nationale Supérieure des Arts Décoratifs in Paris in 1999. He has taught at ENSCI since 2005 and at EnsAD since 2013. His first large project, Mobilier Immobile, consists of nine very large marble pieces.

He drew one object a day for a year and had potters make them as the 365 ceramic pieces of L'Usage des jours, and his first Galerie kreo show in 2019 presented bronze pieces. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them stools, tables, benches and ceiling lamps.
facts: Stools, tables, benches, ceiling lamps (as shown on Formground)

designers:giuseppe-rivadossi.name: Giuseppe Rivadossi
paragraphs: Giuseppe Rivadossi, born in 1935, is an Italian designer and sculptor who works in wood. He grew up in his father's workshop, inherited it in 1962 and gradually turned it into a creative workshop. With his sons Emanuele and Clemente he makes furniture and art pieces from solid blocks of wood, with hand-carved bas-reliefs.
Source Édition lists his Basilio stool and Basilio bench, both dated 1970 and made in solid linden. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Source Édition, a stool and a bench.

designers:guido-venturini.name: Guido Venturini
paragraphs: Guido Venturini was born in Alfonsine, Italy, in 1957. He is an architect and designer working in industrial design, interior design and architecture, and he has taught at Domus Academy and at the Florence Faculty of Architecture.

In 1985 Venturini and Stefano Giovannoni founded the Bolidist group and set up King-Kong Productions. For Alessi he designed the Opus centrepiece, made of 18/10 stainless steel. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them centrepieces, baskets, fruit holders and magnets.
facts: Centrepieces, baskets, fruit holders, stands, bowls, magnets (as shown on Formground)
sources: Alessi: Opus centrepiece by Guido Venturini (designer biography)

designers:hvidt-mlgaard.name: Hvidt & Mølgaard
paragraphs: Hvidt & Mølgaard was a Danish design and architecture studio founded in 1944 by Peter Hvidt (1916-1986) and Orla Mølgaard-Nielsen. Hvidt trained at the Design School in Copenhagen and set up his own studio in 1942. In 1944 he opened Hvidt & Mølgaard, which he ran with Mølgaard-Nielsen until 1975.

The studio designed Portex (1945) and Ax (1950), furniture in laminated technique produced by Fritz Hansen. It also took on architectural assignments, with projects such as the De Danske Sukkerfabrikker building in Copenhagen (1958).
sources: Wikipedia: Peter Hvidt (dates, studio, Portex and Ax, projects)
Danish Wikipedia: Hvidt & Mølgaard (founded 1944, AX chair)

designers:industrial-facility.name: Industrial Facility
paragraphs: Industrial Facility is a London-based design studio co-founded in 2002 by Sam Hecht and Kim Colin. Hecht trained as an industrial designer and Colin as an architect. The studio designs products, furniture and exhibitions for clients including &Tradition, Santa & Cole, Emeco and Wästberg.

Hecht and Colin were appointed European Creative Directors for Muji Japan in 2005, and in 2016 the studio created Future Facility, a department for internet-connected products. On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through &Tradition, among them side chairs and Full Bay shelves, desks and cabinets.
facts: Side chairs, shelves, desks, cabinets, add-ons (as shown on Formground)

designers:inga-sempe.name: Inga Sempé
paragraphs: Inga Sempé is a French designer, born in 1968, who lives and works in Paris. She studied at ENSCI in Paris, graduating in 1993, collaborated with Marc Newson in 1994 and worked with Andrée Putman from 1997 to 1999. From 2000 she collaborated with Cappellini and Edra while establishing her own company in Paris.

Her lamps include the Plissé pendant for Luceplan, made of pleated material that unfolds like an accordion, and a clip lamp for Wästberg. In 2024 the Triennale Milano held the exhibition Inga Sempé, La Casa Imperfetta. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Wästberg, Alessi and nanimarquina, among them table lamps, clamp lamps and cutlery.
facts: Table lamps, clamp lamps, serving cutlery (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Inga Sempé (training, career, works, exhibition)

designers:jacques-biny.name: Jacques Biny
paragraphs: Jacques Biny (1913-1976) was a French interior designer and lighting designer. In 1953 he founded the Luminalite publishing house, which edited lighting models by Jean-Boris Lacroix, Louis Baillon and Michel Buffet.

Luminalite lights have clean lines meant to fit functionally into modern interiors, and Biny was among the first to use materials such as Plexiglas and techniques such as perforated metal and metallic paint. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them wall lights and pendant lights.
facts: Wall lights, pendant lights (as shown on Formground)

designers:jakob-wagner.name: Jakob Wagner
paragraphs: Jakob Wagner was born in Copenhagen in 1963. He took a B.Sc. in design engineering at DIA-M in Denmark in 1987 and a second degree in product design at Art Center in Switzerland in 1992. In 1993 he founded Jakob Wagner Studio in Copenhagen, which began with high-tech products for medical, professional and sports use and later moved into home products.

The studio has made product lines for Alessi, Bang & Olufsen, Menu, Muuto and Stelton, and furniture projects for Cappellini, B&B Italia, Moroso and Hay. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi.

designers:jamie-mclellan.name: Jamie McLellan
paragraphs: Jamie McLellan is a product and furniture designer from New Zealand. He has worked in Milan, Hong Kong and London, including as a senior designer with Tom Dixon, and his work for international clients includes bicycle projects with Avanti and windsurfing design for Neil Pryde.

He works from structure, finding the beauty in the engineering of an object. His Twig coat stand won the HOME New Zealand Designer of the Year title in 2009, and his steel Flyover table, first commissioned for the 2009 Venice Biennale, won it again. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Resident, among them dining tables, chairs, lounge chairs, side tables and storage.
facts: Dining tables, chairs, lounge chairs, side tables, storage (as shown on Formground)

designers:jaume-ramirez.name: Jaume Ramírez
paragraphs: Jaume Ramírez was born in Olot in 1973 and studied design in Girona. He set up his first studio, Zoocreative, in the Basque Country with Gorka Ibargoyen and Josema Carrillo, and has run his own studio in Barcelona since 2019. His first design, the Delica tray collection, earned awards including the Delta de Oro and Red Dot.

He has worked for brands such as Escofet, Normann Copenhagen, Arcos and Mobles 114, and for Marset he designed the Copérnica lamp. On Formground Jaume Ramírez is credited on {count} pieces shown through Marset, among them table, pendant and wall lamps.
facts: Table lamps, pendant lamps, wall lamps (as shown on Formground)

designers:jose-levy.name: José Lévy
paragraphs: José Lévy is a French designer and artist, born in Paris in 1963. He began in fashion, launching his own label in 1990 and later working as artistic director for Cacharel and Ungaro. Since 2007, when his label closed, he has focused on design and the decorative arts.

His collaborations include Manufacture de Sèvres, Hermès and Roche Bobois, and he was a laureate of the Villa Kujoyama in 2011. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through CVL, among them floor lamps, pendants and table lamps.
facts: Floor lamps, pendants, table lamps (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipédia (fr): José Lévy (birth, career, Sèvres, Roche Bobois, Villa Kujoyama 2011)
Carpenters Workshop Gallery: José Lévy (Ungaro, Hermès, Sèvres, Villa Kujoyama)

designers:king-kong.name: King-Kong
paragraphs: King-Kong Productions, also known as King-Kong, is an Italian design studio founded in the mid-1980s by Stefano Giovannoni and Guido Venturini. Giovannoni studied architecture at the University of Florence, graduating in 1978, and was one of the founders of the Bolidist movement.

The studio designed products for companies such as Alessi. Venturini, born in 1957 in Alfonsine, is an Italian architect and designer. On Formground King-Kong is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them baskets, napkin holders, fruit bowls and trivets.
facts: Baskets, napkin holders, fruit bowls, trivets (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Stefano Giovannoni (King-Kong Productions, training, Bolidist)
German Wikipedia: Guido Venturini (birth, King-Kong studio, Alessi)

designers:klenell-sundin.name: Klenell & Sundin
paragraphs: Simon Klenell and Kristoffer Sundin are Swedish designers who both studied at Konstfack in Stockholm. Klenell is known particularly for work in glass, while Sundin has a background in furniture and product design.

For Fogia they designed the Big Sur series in 2017, three coffee tables and a desk made of glass and solid wood. Fogia describes the design as restrained and unpretentious, and lists a coffee table in the series in a smoked glass and smoked oak look.
sources: Fogia: Simon Klenell and Kristoffer Sundin
Fogia: Big Sur Coffee Table Low, Large

designers:komplot-design.name: Komplot Design
paragraphs: Komplot Design is a Copenhagen studio founded in 1987 by the Danish architect Poul Christiansen and the Russian-born designer Boris Berlin. It works in industrial, graphic and furniture design.

Its furniture includes the Gubi chair, the Non rubber chair and the Collage tables, and the Gubi chair is in the permanent collection of MoMA in New York. Clients include Hay, Gubi, Normann Copenhagen and Lightyears. On Formground Komplot Design is credited on {count} pieces shown through Källemo, among them chairs, tables and benches.
facts: Chairs, tables, benches (as shown on Formground)
sources: Komplot Design (own site, address in Copenhagen)

designers:louise-liljencrantz.name: Louise Liljencrantz
paragraphs: Louise Liljencrantz is a Stockholm-based designer who founded her studio in 2009. The studio's interiors work for private and commercial clients focuses on long-lasting, natural materials and good craftsmanship, balancing mid-century influences with a contemporary language.

Alongside interiors she designs furniture and home accessories with simple silhouettes, and has collaborated with KFK Cabinet-Makers on the brands Veermakers and Liljencrantz x K.F.K Master Cabinet Makers. On Formground Louise Liljencrantz is credited on {count} pieces shown through &Tradition, among them lounge chairs, sofas and poufs.
facts: Lounge chair, 3-seater and 2-seater sofas, pouf (as shown on Formground)

designers:lpwk.name: LPWK
paragraphs: LPWK is a design studio that works with Alessi. It was founded and is led by a designer and meta-project designer who graduated from DAMS in Bologna and wrote the book L'officina Alessi, on the first ten years of Alessi's projects with Alessandro Mendini.

In 1990 she was entrusted with running the Alessi Study Centre, an experimental place where professionals and young creatives worked in workshops, and since 2000 the collaboration with Alessi has continued through LPWK. She teaches at Domus Academy and NABA. On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them oil cruets, cheese cellars, figurines and Christmas tree ornaments.
facts: Oil cruets, cheese cellars, ornamental figurines, Christmas tree ornaments (as shown on Formground)

designers:marc-newson.name: Marc Newson
paragraphs: Marc Newson was born in Sydney, Australia, in 1963 and studied fine art at the University of Sydney. He began his career hand-making furniture and timepieces in a workshop in Sydney and held his first solo exhibition in 1986.

Early designs include the Super Guppy Lamp, Pod of Drawers and Embryo Chair, and by the age of 25 he had created the Lockheed Lounge, a riveted aluminium chaise longue. His company, Marc Newson Limited, has been based in the UK since 1997. Galerie kreo represents him and held the solo show Quobus in 2021. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them chairs and lamps.

designers:marco-campardo.name: Marco Campardo
paragraphs: Marco Campardo is a London-based designer, born in 1982, whose practice combines production, research and teaching. His work involves making and material experimentation, using both high-end and lo-fi methods and materials.

Galerie kreo presented his solo show Jello in 2025, and the pieces the gallery lists by him are all from that Jello series. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them side tables, consoles, benches, coffee tables and mirrors.
facts: Side tables, consoles, benches, coffee tables, mirrors (as shown on Formground)

designers:mario-trimarchi.name: Mario Trimarchi
paragraphs: Mario Trimarchi is an Italian designer and architect whose work covers brands, products and artworks. He directed the Master in Design at the Domus Academy from 1990 to 1993, was part of the Olivetti Design Studio, and in 1999 founded the brand design studio FRAGILE, which he led with Frida Doveil.

He designs regularly for Alessi, among other things the Ossidiana coffee maker, which won the Compasso d'Oro, and developed the Swan tap for Hansa and Alessi. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi.

designers:marta-sansoni.name: Marta Sansoni
paragraphs: Marta Sansoni is an architect and designer who lives in Florence, Italy, and graduated in architecture in 1990. That year she took part in the Memory Containers project with Alessi. Her architecture work includes new buildings in Florence and many interiors for homes, shops, restaurants, cafés, wine bars and offices in Italy and abroad.

For Alessi she designed two object families, Cactus! and Ba-Rock, and a series of individual pieces including the Fior d'olio oil pourers. On Formground Marta Sansoni is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them oil cruets and cheese cellars.
facts: Oil cruets, cheese cellars and table accessories (as shown on Formground)

designers:massimo-giacon.name: Massimo Giacon
paragraphs: Massimo Giacon is an Italian comic artist, illustrator and designer, born in Padua in 1961. His comics have appeared in magazines including Frigidaire and Linus, and from 1985 he worked for the Milan studio of Ettore Sottsass.

He has drawn objects and textiles for Memphis and Artemide and watches for Swatch, and between 2000 and 2009 he designed many objects for Alessi. His graphic novel Ettore, published in 2015, is about his friendship with Sottsass. On Formground Giacon is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them ornamental figurines, Christmas tree ornaments and nativities.
facts: Ornamental figurines, Christmas tree ornaments, nativities (as shown on Formground)

designers:mats-theselius.name: Mats Theselius
paragraphs: Mats Theselius is a Swedish furniture designer, born in Stockholm in 1956. He studied interior architecture at Konstfack in Stockholm from 1979 to 1984 and was a professor at the University of Gothenburg's school of design and crafts in 1995 and 1996.

He made his debut in 1986 with an armchair of sheet iron and elk hide, and later designed a glass-fronted bookcase holding 25 volumes of National Geographic, lacquered in the magazine's yellow. Later work includes the Rex, El Rey and Ambassad armchairs and a bishop's cathedra for Linköping Cathedral.
On Formground Mats Theselius is credited on {count} pieces shown through Källemo, among them armchairs, tables, chairs and shelves.
facts: Armchairs, tables, chairs, shelves (as shown on Formground)
sources: Swedish Wikipedia: Mats Theselius (birth, training, works)

designers:michel-boucquillon.name: Michel Boucquillon
paragraphs: Michel Boucquillon was born in Belgium in 1962 and graduated in architecture at Saint-Luc in Brussels in 1986. In 1988 he won the architectural competition for the chamber of the European Parliament in Brussels. In 2000 he opened a second workshop in Lucca, Tuscany, for industrial design and architecture, where he often collaborates with his wife Donia Maaoui.

His clients include Alessi, Artemide, Antoniolupi, Serralunga and Valli&Valli, and in 2017 he won a Nestlé 150th anniversary design competition with Barknest, made with Alessi. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them dog bowls.

designers:michele-de-lucchi.name: Michele De Lucchi
paragraphs: Michele De Lucchi is an Italian architect and designer, born in Ferrara in 1951. He graduated in architecture in Florence and was a prominent figure in the movements Cavart, Studio Alchimia and Memphis. He is the founder of AMDL CIRCLE, a multidisciplinary studio, and was Director of Design for Olivetti from 1988 to 2002.

His products include the First Chair for Memphis (1983), the Tolomeo lamp for Artemide (1986) and the Pulcina espresso maker for Alessi. On Formground Michele De Lucchi is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them pepper and spice grinders, blenders, kitchen scales and small electrical appliances.
facts: Pepper and spice grinders, blenders, kitchen scales, small electrical appliances (as shown on Formground)

designers:miriam-mirri.name: Miriam Mirri
paragraphs: Miriam Mirri is an Italian designer, born in Bologna, who lives and works in Milan. She studied at the Scuola Superiore di Disegno Anatomico and then in design and communication at Università del Progetto, and worked with Branson-Coates Architecture Office in London and with Stefano Giovannoni before opening a practice in 2000.

Her work includes food, wine and coffee objects, pet accessories, watches and furnishings for clients such as Alessi, Mandarina Duck and Seiko. Her Alessi designs include the Big Love spoons and the Lulà pet bowl. Her site lists products, projects and publications.
On Formground Miriam Mirri is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them cups, spoons and bookstands.
facts: Cups, spoons, bookstands (as shown on Formground)

designers:mogens-koch.name: Mogens Koch
paragraphs: Mogens Koch (1898–1992) was a Danish architect and furniture designer, born in Frederiksberg. He studied architecture at the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts, worked for Carl Petersen, Ivar Bentsen and Kaare Klint between 1925 and 1932, and was a professor at the Academy from 1950 to 1968.

He is known for the Book Case (1928), the Folding Chair, and the Wing Chair No. 50 and Armchair No. 51 (1936). On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fredericia, among them bookcases, chairs, objects and cabinets.
facts: Bookcases, chairs, objects, cabinets (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Mogens Koch (life, training, professorship, designs)

designers:naija-ilse.name: Naija Ilsøe
paragraphs: Naija Ilsøe Nielsen is a Danish designer who completed a bachelor's degree in furniture design at VIA University College.

Her KIKU lamp for the Danish brand Frandsen is inspired by Japanese samurai hats. It is made of white linen strings woven into a stainless steel structure, and is available as a table lamp and as a hanging lamp. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Frandsen, among them table lamps, floor lamps and pendants.
facts: Table lamps, floor lamps, pendants (as shown on Formground)
alax.cz (retailer page for the KIKU lamp)
sources: Alax: Frandsen KIKU table lamp (designer, education, materials)

designers:oeo-studio.name: OEO Studio
paragraphs: OEO Studio is a design practice with offices in Copenhagen and Tokyo, founded in 2003 by Thomas Lykke and Anne-Marie Buemann. It works across architecture and interiors, product design, and brand strategy and development.

Its clients span hospitality, lifestyle, product, residential, retail and technology organisations, and its site is oeo.dk. On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through &Tradition and Fredericia, among them benches, coffee tables, dining tables and mirrors.
facts: Benches, coffee tables, dining tables, mirrors, furniture accessories (as shown on Formground)

designers:olivier-gagnere.name: Olivier Gagnère
paragraphs: Olivier Gagnère is a French designer, born in 1952. Galerie kreo describes his work as in harmony with the expert knowledge of artisans in Murano, Arita and Limoges, for unique pieces, limited series and mass production.

His newer collection of mouth-blown vases was conceived in Murano. His work also includes furniture and interior architecture, and the publication Le voyage à Arita covers porcelain, glassware and terracotta. On Formground Olivier Gagnère is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them vases, cups, mirrors and stools.
facts: Vases, cups, mirrors, stools (as shown on Formground)

designers:paola-navone.name: Paola Navone
paragraphs: Paola Navone is an Italian architect and designer, born in Turin in 1950. She graduated in architecture from the Polytechnic University of Turin in 1973 and then moved to Milan. From 1970 to 1980 she worked alongside Alessandro Mendini, Ettore Sottsass and Andrea Branzi in the Alchimia group.

Her work covers product, interior, shop and restaurant design, and her clients have included Driade, Alessi, Knoll International, Cappellini and Armani Casa. In 2023 she organised the exhibition Take It Or Leave It at the Milan Furniture Fair. On Formground Paola Navone is credited on {count} pieces shown through Serax, among them carafes and bottles.
facts: Carafes and bottles (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Paola Navone (birth, training, Alchimia, clients)

designers:paolo-gerosa.name: Paolo Gerosa
paragraphs: Paolo Gerosa is a product and interior designer who graduated in Industrial Design at the Politecnico di Milano. He worked for Baleri Italia in 2006–2007, and from 2008 to 2011 collaborated with LPWK Studio of Laura Polinoro on design and meta-design of products, mostly for Alessi.

Since 2010 he has designed objects, furniture, complements and lamps for international brands. In 2011 he opened his own studio for product and interior design, and since 2014 he has been with Esprit Architettura Architetti Associati in Bergamo, Italy, working on architectural projects. On Formground Paolo Gerosa is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi.
sources: Paolo Gerosa Design Studio: Pills of me (biography)

designers:paolo-rizzatto.name: Paolo Rizzatto
paragraphs: Paolo Rizzatto is an architect and designer, born in Milan in 1941. He graduated in architecture from the Milan Polytechnic in 1965 and in 1978 founded Luceplan with Riccardo Sarfatti and Sandra Severi; he later designed the Luceplan factory and headquarters in Milan.

His architectural works include a nursery school in Segrate and a retirement home in Galliate. He has received the Compasso d'Oro several times, from 1981 to 2011, and his work is held by museums including MoMA in New York and the Victoria and Albert Museum in London.
On Formground Paolo Rizzatto is credited on {count} pieces shown through Ghidini 1961, among them dining tables, chairs, cabinets and armchairs.
facts: Dining tables, chairs, cabinets, armchairs (as shown on Formground)
sources: Italian Embassy in Washington: Paolo Rizzatto

designers:peter-andersson.name: Peter Andersson
paragraphs: Peter Andersson, born in 1970, graduated from Konstfack in Stockholm in 1999 and founded Peter Andersson Studio (PAS) the same year. The studio works from Stockholm and southern Sweden and designs furniture for care and education settings, including the Tilt chair and other seating for NC Nordic Care.

For Källemo he and Matti Klenell extended an earlier Botero chair into the Botero sofa. He also designed the Corso easy chair for Lammhults, and his pieces are held by the Nationalmuseum. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Källemo, among them chairs and sofas.
facts: Stockholm (studio works from Stockholm and southern Sweden)
sources: Scandinavian Design: Peter Andersson, Making the Ordinary Less Ordinary

designers:pierre-paulin.name: Pierre Paulin
paragraphs: Pierre Paulin (1927–2009) was a French designer who graduated from Camondo in Paris and began his career in the workshop of Marcel Gascoin. He worked with Thonet France, Meubles TV, Disderot and above all the Dutch manufacturer Artifort, which produced the Ribbon Chair (F 582, 1966).

He developed a way of covering seats with colourful elastic fabric, and from 1968 worked with the Mobilier national, designing the interiors of the Denon wing at the Louvre. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them armchairs, coffee tables and chairs.
facts: Armchairs, coffee tables, chairs (as shown on Formground)

designers:playlab.name: PlayLab
paragraphs: PlayLab is a creative agency cofounded in 2009 by Archie Lee Coates IV and Jeff Franklin, who met while studying architecture at Virginia Tech. The office moved to Los Angeles in 2020.

Its work includes installations and runway shows, among them Louis Vuitton runways for Virgil Abloh, the + POOL project in New York's East River, the architecture journal Clog and an installation for Alessi at Milan Design Week 2024. On Formground PlayLab is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them Christmas tree ornaments and wall decorations.
facts: Christmas tree ornaments, wall decorations (as shown on Formground)

designers:pucci-de-rossi.name: Pucci de Rossi
paragraphs: Pucci de Rossi (1947–2013) was an Italian artist and a student of the American sculptor H.B. Walker. He began his artistic career in 1971 working in cut metal and later reclaimed wood, and moved to France in 1977.

His creations embody the 1980s "Furniture Sculpture" trend: ironic and offbeat, yet functional. He called himself a "fake designer", according to Galerie Kreo. In 2012 he worked with the Sèvres national manufactory on the Écrous et Boulons vase. On Formground Pucci de Rossi is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them floor lamps.

designers:radice-orlandini.name: Radice Orlandini
paragraphs: Radice Orlandini is the design duo of Andrea Radice and Folco Orlandini, who graduated from the Politecnico di Milano, Radice in industrial design and Orlandini in architecture. They began working together in 2008 and approach each project through three ideas: paternity, irony and improvement on what already exists.

Since 2008 the studio has designed products for furniture companies including Calligaris, Skitsch and Quinti Sedute, and the Kin and Paloma chairs for Baleri Italia. On Formground Radice Orlandini are credited on {count} pieces shown through Baleri Italia, among them chairs, armchairs and stools.
facts: Stackable chair, armchair, chair with armrests, kitchen stool, bar stool (as shown on Formground)

designers:richard-hutten.name: Richard Hutten
paragraphs: Richard Hutten is a Dutch designer, born in 1967, who graduated from the Design Academy Eindhoven in 1991 and then started his own studio in Rotterdam. He has been involved with Droog Design since its start in 1993 and is known for functional, conceptual and humorous furniture he calls "No sign of design". He designed the seating at Schiphol Airport using recycled, recyclable or biodegradable materials. His site lists the Dandelion Lamp for Moooi, the X-chair for Moroso and the Butterfly design for Ghidini 1961.
On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Ghidini 1961, among them rugs, chairs, stools, armchairs and shelving.
facts: Rugs, chairs, stools, armchairs, shelving (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Richard Hutten (education, studio, Droog, Schiphol)

designers:richard-sapper.name: Richard Sapper
paragraphs: Richard Sapper (1932–2015) was a German industrial designer, born in Munich, who was based in Milan for much of his career. He began in the styling department at Mercedes-Benz in Stuttgart and moved to Milan in 1958. His best-known designs include the Tizio desk lamp for Artemide (1972) and radios and televisions for Brionvega with Marco Zanuso.

Alessi commissioned him in 1978 for the 9090 stove-top espresso maker, followed by the Bollitore kettle (1984) and the Todo cheese grater (2006). On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi, among them espresso coffee makers, saucepans, a cheese grater and a flambé lamp.
facts: Espresso coffee makers, saucepans, cheese grater, flambé lamp (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia: Richard Sapper (life, Milan career, Tizio, Alessi designs)

designers:robert-mathieu.name: Robert Mathieu
paragraphs: Robert Mathieu (1921-2002) was a French lighting designer. He trained at the Ecole Boulle, worked as a watchmaker and in 1949 opened his first lighting shop, later expanding to three in Paris.

His eponymous house also produced works by designers including Michel Buffet and Jean-Boris Lacroix. Mathieu called his own pieces "rational lighting", putting function before form. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them floor lamps.

designers:robert-stadler.name: Robert Stadler
paragraphs: Robert Stadler was born in Vienna in 1966 and studied design at IED in Milan and ENSCI in Paris. In 1992 he cofounded the Radi Designers group, which was active until 2008 and made limited edition pieces for Galerie kreo as well as industrial design commissions for Air France and Moulinex. In 2001 he set up his own design studio in Paris.

He has worked for clients such as Drucker, Fabbian, Ghidini 1961, Hermès, Thonet and Vitra, and his work is in collections including the Centre Pompidou and the Vitra Design Museum. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Ghidini 1961, among them cabinets, ottomans, shelving, sofas and armchairs.
facts: Cabinets, ottomans, shelving, sofas, armchairs (as shown on Formground)

designers:roderick-vos.name: Roderick Vos
paragraphs: Roderick Vos was born in Groningen, the Netherlands, in 1965 and began studying industrial design at Design Academy Eindhoven in 1984. After graduating in 1990 together with his partner Claire Vos, he moved to Surabaya, Indonesia, to develop their knowledge of rattan furniture and textile production. In 1999 they started the design office Studio Roderick Vos, now based in Nijmegen.

The studio works mainly in lighting, textile, accessories and furniture for international design labels such as Moooi and Pode, and several of its works have been acquired by museums including Stedelijk Amsterdam. On Formground Roderick Vos is credited on {count} pieces shown through Pode, among them sofas, corner sofas and armchairs.
facts: Sofas, corner sofas, armchairs (as shown on Formground)

designers:roger-capron.name: Roger Capron
paragraphs: Roger Capron (1922–2006) was a French designer who worked in ceramics and studied at the École des Arts Appliqués in Paris. In 1946 he settled in Vallauris, where he created the ceramic workshop Callis, and in 1952 he founded Atelier Capron, a small factory that employed about fifty workers.

His signature was using earthenware tiles or enamelled lava, traditionally made for decorative panels, in furniture and objects. Works are shown at the Musée national de la Céramique in Sèvres and the Musée Magnelli in Vallauris. On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them coffee tables and tables.
facts: Coffee tables, tables (as shown on Formground)

designers:ron-arad.name: Ron Arad
paragraphs: Ron Arad is a British-Israeli industrial designer, artist and architectural designer, born in Tel Aviv in 1951, who lives and works in Camden, north London. He studied at the Bezalel Academy of Arts and Design in Jerusalem and then at the Architectural Association School of Architecture in London.

In 1981 he co-founded the design and production studio One Off with Caroline Thorman. Ron Arad Associates was formed in 1989, and Ron Arad Architects in 2008. His furniture includes the Rover chair, the Bookworm shelf produced by Kartell and the Tom Vac chair, and he has also designed for Alessi. On Formground Ron Arad is credited on {count} pieces shown through Alessi.

designers:samy-rio.name: Samy Rio
paragraphs: Samy Rio is a French designer born in 1989. He studied woodwork for four years before training in industrial design at ENSCI-Les Ateliers in Paris, graduating in 2014 with research on the industrialisation of bamboo tubes.

That project won the Grand Prix of Design Parade 10 at Villa Noailles in 2015. He has since done residencies at the Cirva in Marseille, the ceramic city of Sèvres and the NTCRI in Taiwan, working across glass, ceramics, wood and bamboo, and began collaborating with Galerie Kreo. On Formground Samy Rio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them mirrors.

designers:sergei-grigorev.name: Sergei Grigorev
paragraphs: Sergei Grigorev is a designer based in Cyprus who runs 20by8 (Twentybyeight), a small workshop that makes chairs, mostly, and other objects. After working for many years as an interior designer, Grigorev started the workshop to turn ideas into objects.

Pieces are produced by hand in small batches, with a focus on high-end craftsmanship, distinctive design and premium materials, and Grigorev is responsible for each piece from the first sketch to the last stitch. On Formground Grigorev is credited on {count} pieces shown through 20by8, among them chairs, bar stools and armchairs. The workshop's site has pages for works, info and inquiries.
facts: Chairs, bar stools, armchairs (as shown on Formground)

designers:signe-hytte.name: Signe Hytte
paragraphs: Signe Hytte is a Danish designer based in Copenhagen who studied at Aarhus University and at TEKO Design and Business School. Hytte was Head of Design at the Danish brand &Tradition and afterwards founded Signe Hytte Studio.

The Journey lighting collection for &Tradition, with table and floor lamps, takes basic shapes such as spheres and rectangles as its starting point. On Formground Signe Hytte is credited on {count} pieces shown through &Tradition, among them floor, table and wall lamps.
facts: Floor lamps, table lamps, wall lamps (as shown on Formground)
sources: smow: Signe Hytte (training, role at &Tradition, Journey collection)

designers:sissel-gram-warringa.name: Sissel Gram Warringa
paragraphs: Sissel Gram Warringa is a Danish designer. After a Carpentry Foundation programme at KTS in Copenhagen in 2016, she graduated with a First Class BA (Hons) in Product and Furniture Design from Kingston School of Art in London in 2020.

Furniture, kitchenware and lights are among her most common designs, according to Alax. For Frandsen she designed the Peel collection of pendant, table and wall lamps, made from a single sheet of cut stainless steel. On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through Frandsen, among them table lamps, wall lamps and pendants.
facts: Table lamps, wall lamps, pendants (as shown on Formground)

designers:studio-wieki-somers.name: Studio Wieki Somers
paragraphs: Studio Wieki Somers is the name under which Dutch designer Wieki Somers works together with Dylan van den Berg. Somers graduated from the Design Academy Eindhoven in 2000 and has taught there. Her work takes everyday items and realises them anew with foreign material, form, technology or function.

Known designs include the Bathboat, a bathtub shaped like a rowing boat, and the Bellflower, a two-metre-tall lamp woven out of a single piece of fabric. In October 2009 the studio won the Golden Eye at the Dutch Design Awards with the Merry-go-round Coat Rack, designed for the cloakroom of Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen. On Formground the studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them vases and tables.

designers:sybilla.name: Sybilla
paragraphs: Sybilla is a fashion designer, born in New York in 1963 and resident in Spain. She presented her first collection in Madrid in 1983 and later opened shops in Madrid and Paris. Her work has extended beyond clothes to furniture and ceramics, including candles with sinuous forms made with the Catalan candle maker Cerabella. In 2014 she was awarded the Gold Medal of Merit in the Fine Arts. Her own site, sybilla.com, is an online shop.
On Formground she is credited on {count} pieces shown through nanimarquina, among them indoor rugs.
sources: Wikipedia (Spanish): Sybilla (birth, first collection, shops, candles, 2014 medal)

designers:sylvain-willenz.name: Sylvain Willenz
paragraphs: Sylvain Willenz is a designer born in Brussels in 1978. Willenz completed an MA in Design Products at the Royal College of Art in London in 2003 and opened a design office in Brussels the following year.

The work spans furniture, lighting, textiles and prints, along with limited-edition projects for galleries and private clients. Clients listed on the studio's site include HAY, Muuto, Kvadrat, Cappellini and Serax. On Formground Willenz is credited on {count} pieces shown through CVL, among them pendants, wall lamps and chandeliers.
facts: Pendants, wall lamps, chandeliers (as shown on Formground)

designers:tadaima.name: Tadaima
paragraphs: Tadaima is a design studio and creative practice founded in Copenhagen in 2021 by Hanne, Josefine and Emma Berzant, who have backgrounds in photography, product design and creative direction. The name is Japanese for "I'm home", and the studio draws on Scandinavian, Italian and Japanese influences.

Alongside curating products, it made its debut as a designer through a collaboration with Fredericia: two hand-blown glass vases, a cushion and a throw, crafted in Europe. On Formground Tadaima is credited on {count} pieces shown through Fredericia, among them vases.

designers:taf-studio.name: TAF Studio
paragraphs: TAF Studio is a Stockholm-based design studio that has worked with Nordic manufacturers. Its Atelier Chair for the Finnish brand Artek is a compact, lightweight wooden chair; 245 of them have furnished the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm since its reopening in October 2018.

Other work listed on Scandinavian Design includes the Museum Candle Holder and the Museum Trolley for String Furniture, and the Rime chandelier, a glass pendant for Muuto. On Formground TAF Studio is credited on {count} pieces shown through Gärsnäs, among them tables.
sources: Scandinavian Design: Atelier Chair by TAF Studio

designers:tejo-remy.name: Tejo Remy
paragraphs: Tejo Remy is a Dutch designer of products, interiors and public space, born in Nijmegen in 1960 and educated in Utrecht. He has designed for Droog Design since 1991, when his chest of drawers You Can't Lay Down Your Memory and his Rag Chair became part of the first Droog collection. Reuse of existing products is central to both. Since 2000 he has worked with René Veenhuizen as Remy & Veenhuizen, and the Centraal Museum in Utrecht holds his designs.
On Formground he is credited on {count} pieces shown through Galerie Kreo, among them chests of drawers and chairs.
facts: Chests of drawers, chairs (as shown on Formground)
sources: Wikipedia (Dutch): Tejo Remy (birth, training, Droog Design, Remy & Veenhuizen)
Galerie Kreo: Tejo Remy (Utrecht, Droog Design founding designer)

designers:thijs-prinsen.name: Thijs Prinsen
paragraphs: Thijs Prinsen is an architect, born in 1984, who received his architect diploma from the Provinciale Hogeschool Limburg in 2007. Prinsen has worked at Lens°ass Architects since then, became a partner in 2012 and now leads the practice.

For Serax, Prinsen designed a collection of wall lamps that reflects his architectural signature. They have rectangular shapes in coloured concrete and terracotta, inspired by reclaimed bricks from a renovation project. On Formground Prinsen is credited on {count} pieces shown through Serax, all wall lamps.

designers:thomas-albertsen.name: Thomas Albertsen
paragraphs: Thomas Albertsen was educated at the Danish Design Academy in 2007 and has worked as a designer ever since. According to Frandsen, his lighting designs focus on good light and forms that are simple, yet interesting and special. Frandsen is based in Horsens, Denmark.

Albertsen designed Grasp, a portable lamp for Frandsen that became a runner-up on the Danish TV show Denmark's Next Classic; the Frandsen page also says he was chosen as the winner of the 2023 edition of the program for his designs. On Formground Albertsen is credited on {count} pieces shown through Frandsen, among them wall lamps, table lamps, pendants and outdoor lamps.
facts: Wall lamps, table lamps, pendants, outdoor lamps (as shown on Formground)

designers:toan-nguyen.name: Toan Nguyen
paragraphs: Toan Nguyen is a designer who graduated from ENSCI in Paris in 1995. He trained with Alberto Lievore in Barcelona and moved to Milan in 1996, where he became head of Antonio Citterio's design department.

In 2009 he founded his own studio in Milan, collaborating with brands across Europe, North America and Asia on furniture, lighting, ceramics and technology. Vibia's page for him features the Algorithm lighting. On Formground Toan Nguyen is credited on {count} pieces shown through Vibia, among them pendants.

designers:thamvidegard.name: Tham & Videgård
paragraphs: Tham & Videgård is a Stockholm architecture practice, registered as ThamVidegård Arkitekter AB. It was founded in 1999 by Bolle Tham and Martin Videgård, and its team numbers 18 people.

The studio describes its approach as experimental, with a focus on lasting quality and architectural integrity. Its portfolio includes the Stockholm Concert Hall, the Düsseldorf Opera, the Kalmar Museum of Art and the Tree Hotel, where its Mirrorcube won a Design S award from Cappellini. The studio's site shows its projects.
